She must either retain him or remain unmarried; that is, she must not accept another bishop while her own is alive, lest she incur the charge of fornication or adultery.

For if she has committed adultery—that is, if she has joined herself to another bishop, or brought another bishop over herself, or caused or desired him to be appointed—then, through the most severe penance, she must either be reconciled to her own bishop or remain unmarried [Col. 0084D]. Hence the Lord also says in the Gospel: “Whoever looks at a woman in order to lust after her has already committed adultery with her in his heart” (Matt. 5:28).

A bishop ought to teach his Church suitably and without interruption, and wisely govern and love her, so that she may abstain from vices and be able to attain eternal salvation. And she ought to receive his teaching with such great reverence, and love and cherish him as God’s ambassador and herald of the truth, because, as the Truth bears witness: “Whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven” (Matt. 16:19).

This sentence, brothers, is greatly to be feared, and you must take care lest you offend those who have received such authority from the Lord [Col. 0085B]. Therefore they must rather be obeyed, loved, and supremely venerated—not slandered, torn apart, or expelled, but supported and loved—for the Lord himself says: “Whoever hears you hears me, and whoever despises you despises me” (Luke 10:16).

For this reason we write these things to you and to all the faithful, brothers, so that you may guard yourselves against such conduct and leave your descendants not a bad example but a good one, since an injury done to bishops concerns Christ, in whose place they serve.

For we have heard that certain bishops among you have been defamed and torn apart, and driven from their own cities, while others have been appointed in those same cities while the former were still alive. Yet bishops cannot be established elsewhere except in cities that are not insignificant. Therefore we write these things to you so that you may know that this is not permitted, but that the rightful bishops must be recalled and restored in complete integrity. Those, however, who hold their brides—which we understand, by the established arrangement, to be their wives—to an adulterous disgrace shall be expelled as adulterers and branded as infamous; and we command that they be barred from ecclesiastical honors.

If you have any complaint against them, then, after these matters have been dealt with, it must be investigated and settled by the authority of this holy See. And, not to discuss everything individually now, charity will teach you to do every good thing—if charity itself is present in you—for just as charity teaches such conduct, hatred teaches those who are estranged from salvation to do every evil.

Therefore, as true disciples of God, first cast discord and the dissensions of others out of your hearts, for from these every evil work proceeds, and preserve kindness and simplicity with your whole mind [Col. 0085D].

Nevertheless, let all of you know that the bishop labors above all of you, because each of you bears his own labor, whereas he bears both his own and that of each individual. Therefore, just as he labors for all of you, so you must all labor most earnestly for him, so much so that, if necessary, you should lay down your lives for him, just as he ought, if necessary, to lay down his life for you. The Savior himself says: “The good shepherd gives his life for his sheep” (John 10:11). You, for your part, obey them and keep watch for them, because they keep watch for you, as those who will have to render an account for your souls, so that they may do this with joy and not with groaning.

[Col. 0086A]

A bishop must not be challenged or accused by the common people or by ordinary persons, even if he is disorderly, because God disposes the life of rulers according to the merits of their subjects, as in the example of the sinful David, compared with rulers who transgress because of the merit of the people. Priests ought to investigate the sins of the peoples and examine each person with vigilant care, according to the testimony of the Lord who speaks to Jeremiah: “I have appointed you as a tested examiner of my people, and you shall know and test their way” (Jer. 6:27).

I say this because the enemy very often turns good into evil and places a stain upon the elect. Therefore, if there are any revilers or accusers of bishops or of other priests, they ought not to be heard by the judges of the Church before their suspicion or reputation has been examined: with what intention, faith, truthfulness, manner of life, conscience, and merit they have undertaken these things; whether for God, or for empty glory, or from enmity, hatred, or greed. All these matters must be faithfully investigated and carefully examined.

For there are some who perversely reproach their superiors if they have caused them even a little inconvenience. For this reason the primates of the Churches must look carefully to it that none of their innocent subjects is harassed or scandalized, keeping in mind the Lord’s sentence: “Whoever causes one of these little ones to stumble, it would be better for him to have a millstone hung around his neck and to be drowned in the depths of the sea” (Matt. 18:6), and so forth.

Almighty God, moreover, in order to restrain us from approving a hasty judgment—since all things are naked and open to his eyes—nevertheless did not wish to judge the evils of Sodom on hearsay before he had clearly established what was being said. Hence he himself says: “I will go down and see whether they have completed in action the outcry that has come to me, or whether it is not so, that I may know” (Gen. 18:21).

Almighty God, to whom nothing is hidden and before whom all things are manifest even before they occur, deigned to investigate this and many other matters himself—not for any other reason, since we have omitted the rest here to avoid prolixity, than to give us an example, so that we would not be hasty in examining and judging matters, and so that no one would presume to believe the evils of some person before testing them.

By his example we are warned never to be hasty in pronouncing sentence, or to judge anything rashly, carelessly, and without examination, as the voice of Truth says: “Do not judge, so that you may not be judged; for with whatever judgment you judge, you will be judged” (Matt. 7:1), and so forth.

Therefore, let no one be moved by evils that have merely been heard, and let no one ever believe things said indiscriminately without certain proof. Rather, let him carefully investigate what he has heard beforehand, lest anyone act precipitately.

If the Lord of all, though knowing everything, did not wish to believe or judge the evils of all the Sodomites—whose outcry had reached heaven—before he himself had carefully investigated with trustworthy witnesses what he had heard and had truly learned it from their deeds, how much more ought we, human beings and sinners, to guard against this and judge or condemn no one before true and just proof? The Apostle Paul plainly says: “Who are you to judge another’s servant? He will stand or fall before his own master” (Rom. 14:4).

Hence the Lord also speaks through the prophet David: “Do not exalt your horn on high” (Ps. 74:6), speaking with an arrogant neck; for it is neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the desert of the mountains, but God is judge: he humbles one and exalts another. For there is a cup in the Lord’s hand, full of unmixed wine; he pours it out, and all the wicked of the earth shall drink its dregs. But I will proclaim forever; I will sing praise to the God of Jacob.

And elsewhere the same Prophet says: “At your rebuke, O God of Jacob” (Ps. 75:7), both chariot and horse fell into deep sleep. You are terrible, and who can stand before you? From that moment your wrath came; from heaven you pronounced judgment. The earth was afraid and fell silent when God arose for judgment, to save all the meek of the earth.

The Apostle says: “Vengeance is mine; I will repay” (Rom. 12:19). And elsewhere the same Apostle says: “The rebuke administered by the majority is sufficient, so that you should rather forgive and console him, lest perhaps the one who is in distress be swallowed up by excessive sorrow. Therefore I urge you to confirm your love for him” (2 Cor. 2:6).

And the Lord says in the Gospel: “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your strength, and your neighbor as yourself” (Luke 10:27). For love of one’s neighbor does no evil.

Therefore, according to the Apostle, you are without excuse, O every human being who judges; for in judging another you condemn yourself, since you do the very things that you judge. We know that God’s judgment is according to truth against those who do such things.

Do you suppose, O human being, who judges those who do such things and yourself do them, that you will escape God’s judgment? Or do you despise the riches of his goodness, patience, and long-suffering? Do you not know that God’s kindness leads you to repentance? But according to your hardness and unrepentant heart, you are storing up wrath for yourself on the day of wrath and the revelation of God’s righteous judgment, who will repay each person according to his works:

to those who, by perseverance in good work, seek glory, honor, and incorruption: eternal life;

but to those who are contentious and do not obey the truth, yet believe in iniquity: wrath and indignation, tribulation and distress for every human soul that does evil, for the Jew first and also for the Greek.

But glory, honor, and peace for everyone who does good.

And elsewhere the same Apostle says: “We have already charged that all are under sin, as it is written: There is no one who is righteous; there is no one who understands; there is no one who seeks God. All have turned aside; together they have become useless. There is no one who does good, not even one. Their throat is an open grave; with their tongues they have acted deceitfully. The poison of asps is under their lips. Their mouth is full of cursing and bitterness. Their feet are swift to shed blood; destruction and misery are in their ways, and they have not known the way of peace. There is no fear of God before their eyes.

“Now we know that whatever the law says, it speaks to those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be stopped and the whole world may become subject to God. For no flesh will be justified before him by works of the law; through the law comes knowledge of sin.

“But now the righteousness of God has been manifested apart from the law, attested by the law and the prophets: the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ for all who believe. For there is no distinction. All have sinned and lack the glory of God, being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus. God set him forth as an expiation through faith in his blood, to demonstrate his righteousness because of the remission of former sins, in the forbearance of God, to demonstrate his righteousness at the present time, so that he himself might be righteous and justify the one who has faith in Jesus Christ” (Rom. 3:3).

Again, the same Apostle says: “Who will bring an accusation against God’s elect? God, who justifies? Who is he who condemns? Christ Jesus, who died—indeed, who also rose again—who is at the right hand of God and who also intercedes for us. Who, then, will separate us from the love of Christ? Tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or danger, or the sword? As it is written: Because of you we are put to death all day long; we are considered like sheep for slaughter. But in all these things we prevail through him who loved us.

“For I am certain that neither death nor life, neither angels nor principalities nor powers, neither things present nor things to come, neither strength nor height nor depth nor any other creature will be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord” (Rom. 8:33).

We ought, as the same Apostle says, to bear the weaknesses of the weak as the stronger, and not to please ourselves. Let each of you please his neighbor for the good, for edification. For Christ did not please himself, but, as it is written: “The reproaches of those who reproached you fell upon me” (Rom. 15:1).

“Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and God of all consolation, who consoles us in all our tribulation, so that we too may be able to console those who are in every distress through the consolation with which we ourselves are consoled by God. For just as the sufferings of Christ abound in us, so also through Christ our consolation abounds.

“Whether we are afflicted for your consolation and salvation, or whether we are consoled for your consolation, which works in you endurance of the same sufferings that we also suffer, our hope for you is firm, knowing that just as you are companions in suffering, so also you will be companions in consolation” (2 Cor. 1:3).

“God is faithful, and he will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you can bear; but with the temptation he will also provide a way out, so that you may be able to endure” (1 Cor. 10:13).

Therefore, dearest ones, pursue love for one another, strive after better and spiritual things, and help one another, so that you may always be able to please God in all things. May the God of peace be with all of you.

[Col. 0090A] Amen. Given on the Kalends of November, Gallio and Bradua CC.

## The Decrees of Alexander I, Pope, Begin

On priests not being harassed, nor writings being extorted from them through fear or any fraud; on the Lord’s Passion being mingled with the consecration of his body; on water mixed with salt being blessed for the people; and on the faith of the holy Trinity.

(In the year of the Lord 119, under the emperor Hadrian.)

[Col. 0089]

[Col. 0089B]

Alexander, bishop, to all the orthodox serving the Lord Christ throughout the various provinces, greetings.

As we consider the fear of divine judgment, dearest brothers, and that after this life each person will receive according to what he has done, it has not been lawful for us to remain silent about what may become a matter of accusation; necessity has compelled us to speak to you, as the prophet says: “Raise your voice like a trumpet” (Isa. 58:1). Since the care of all the Churches has been entrusted to me, if I remain silent I shall hear the Lord say: “You have rejected the commandment of God in order to establish your own traditions.”

For what else is it to reject God’s commandment than to delight too freely in establishing new things according to private counsel and human judgment? Hence it is written elsewhere: “Do not cross the ancient boundaries that your fathers established” (Prov. 22:28). Whoever postpones and confounds the decrees of the Fathers unquestionably crosses those boundaries [Col. 0089C].

For it has come to the awareness of the Apostolic See that there are certain men so foolish that they do not at all observe the Lord’s commands or the statutes of the apostles and their successors. They not only do not hesitate to touch those of whom the Lord says, “Whoever touches you touches the apple of my eye” (Zech. 2:8), but are not even afraid to persecute them.

And although they persecute us—for they can persecute neither us without themselves nor themselves without us, since we are disciples of the one who commanded us to lay down our lives for our brothers—we have nevertheless not dared to conceal from them the dangers and destruction that threaten them, lest we be condemned by the prophetic sentence—which God forbid—which says: “If you announce his iniquity to the wicked, you have saved your own soul. But if you do not announce it to him, I will require his blood from your hand” (Ezek. 3:19).

This too has been reported to this holy See—a thing shameful to say and hostile not only to the priestly name but also to every Christian name: namely, that some people compel certain bishops or priests through fear, extort things from them by force, or deceive them by fraud, causing them to write and authenticate with their own hands, and to recite and acknowledge before the people, certain statements of their confession directed toward a different position from the one they ought to hold; or statements made because their own affairs have not been investigated; or, worse still, writings supporting the sect of another’s error.

Some are said to be shut up in prisons and workhouses, so that, terrified at least by these plots, the Lord’s priests may turn aside and favor the will of their persecutors.

It has further been reported to the summit of this holy and apostolic See—to which the ordering of the most important causes and the affairs of all the Churches have been entrusted by the Lord himself, as to the head—since he said to Peter, the chief of the apostles: “You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church” (Matt. 16:18)—that certain rivals of Christ and plotters against his holy Church dare to accuse God’s priests before public judges, although the Apostle rather commands that Christians’ cases be brought before the Churches and settled there.

Those who transgress in this way have transgressed against their Lord and do not obey his commands. Of them the Lord speaks through the prophet Hosea, saying: “They have turned aside like wanton cows” (Hos. 4:16), and they have loved to bring disgrace upon their protectors.

And again he says:

“Woe to them, because they have departed from me; they will be devastated, because they have transgressed against me. I redeemed them, and they have spoken lies against me. They did not cry out to me in their heart, but they howled upon their beds; they ruminated over grain and wine, and they departed from me. I instructed them and strengthened their arms, yet they devised evil against me. They returned to being without a yoke; they became like a deceitful bow” (Hos. 7:13).

“The Lord will cast them away,” says the same prophet, “because they did not listen to him, and they will be wanderers among the nations” (Hos. 9:17).

This concerns those clerics or laypeople who accuse bishops or other priests before either their primates or other judges, rather than bringing their complaints to the ears of those whom they believe have wronged them, so that they may receive from them either their right or a just explanation.

Again, through the same prophet the Lord says:

“Hear this, house of Israel, and listen, house of the king; pay attention, priests, because judgment is against you. For you have become a snare to the watchtower and a net spread over Tabor, and you have turned victims aside into the depths” (Hos. 5:1).

And I am the instructor of you all.

Elsewhere he says: “All of you have become hot like an oven, because you devour your judges” (Hos. 7:7).

They turn the Lord’s victims into the depths when they devour or unjustly tear apart those who are called the Lord’s eyes. For if someone today were to tear out or remove the eyes of a secular prince, would he be guilty of treason or not? Surely he would either be handed over to death or branded with perpetual infamy.

If such things are done by human beings against the powers of this world, what do you think should be done on behalf of those of whom the Lord says: “Whoever touches you touches the apple of my eye” (Zech. 2:8)?

Without doubt, those who persecute them and unjustly strive to remove them from office, contrary to apostolic authority, are to be prevented from death if the Lord’s words are observed: “I do not desire the death of the sinner, but that he should turn and live” (Ezek. 33:11). Nevertheless, they are branded with perpetual infamy and judged worthy of exile to a neighboring region.

Concerning such people, from the time of the apostles and thereafter, we possess these traditions and decrees by which we close their mouths against accusing bishops or giving testimony against them. We know that such accusers are dead—not through human acts, but through divine acts. Of them the Lord speaks through the same prophet:

“Ephraim, oppressed by slander, has been crushed by judgment, because he began to follow filth. I am like a moth to Ephraim and like rottenness to the house of Judah. Ephraim saw his sickness and Judah his wound; Ephraim went to Assyria and sent to the avenging king, but he will not be able to heal you or release the bond from you” (Hos. 5:11).

Those who pursue bishops with sacrilegious persuasion and strive to tear them apart—or those who rightly offer sacrifice to the Lord—undoubtedly persecute and tear apart the one whose place they occupy. Hence the Lord says through the prophet Joel:

“Have you repaid me with vengeance? And if you take revenge against me, I will quickly and speedily return your recompense upon your own heads” (Joel 3:4).

And through the prophet Hosea the Lord says: “Who is wise and will understand these things, intelligent and will know them? For the ways of the Lord are upright, and the righteous will walk in them” (Hos. 14:10), but transgressors will fall in them.

Truth itself also says: “Whoever hears you hears me, and whoever despises you despises me” (Luke 10:16).

Supported by these and many other commands of the Lord, and avoiding the destruction of human beings, we prohibit such things together with all the members of this holy See, which the Lord has established as the head of the whole Church, lest the Lord’s people be confounded forever.

For we also read that our predecessors forbade anyone to grieve teachers or to receive an accusation against them. The chief of the apostles himself, instructing the people at the ordination of blessed Clement, said: “Whoever grieves a teacher of the truth sins against Christ and provokes God, the Father of all; therefore he will be deprived of life.”

And the teacher of the nations says: “If someone is overtaken in any transgression, you who are spiritual should restore such a person in a spirit of gentleness, considering yourself, lest you too be tempted. Bear one another’s burdens, and so you will fulfill the law of Christ” (Gal. 6:1).

[Col. 0091D]

Considering these acts of mercy and avoiding dangers to souls, together with all the priests of the Lord who have gathered with us in this sacred city, and with all the members of this head, we establish and decree, as we have received from the blessed apostles, the other holy Fathers, and their successors, that all who persecute the holy Fathers, or openly strive to remove or tear them apart, are to be infamous and made strangers to the thresholds of the Church until they have given satisfaction [Col. 0092A].

For God hates those who arm themselves against fathers as invaders or destroyers of fathers. They are made infamous because they persecute fathers.

If those against whom the greatest teachers—we call them bishops—are opposed because of their crimes are not even permitted to speak, how much less should those who harass them be agreed with or spoken to, lest people be found to share in their crimes. For not only those who do such things, but also those who consent to those who do them, are guilty.

Therefore the blessed chief of the apostles, Peter, instructing the clergy and people at the ordination of our holy predecessor Clement, said:

“If Clement is an enemy to anyone because of his actions, do not wait for him to say to you, ‘Do not be friends with that person.’ Rather, you must observe the matter wisely, obey his will without sharing in the other person’s conduct, and turn away from the one whom you perceive to be opposed by him. Nor should you speak to those to whom he does not speak. Thus, whoever is at fault, while desiring to retain the friendship of all of you, should hasten to be reconciled to the one who presides over all, so that through this he may return to salvation once he has begun to obey the commands of his superior.

“But if anyone is a friend to those to whom he is not a friend, and speaks with those to whom he does not speak, he too is one of those who wish to destroy the Church of God. Although he may appear to be with you in body, in mind and spirit he is against you. Such an enemy is much worse than those who are outside and are openly hostile. For under the appearance of friendship he pursues what is hostile, and he scatters and devastates the Church.”

Likewise, if writings of any kind have been extorted from such persons through fear, fraud, or force, or if they have been written or authenticated by them in any way as a means of freeing themselves, we decree that they shall bring them no prejudice or harm. Nor, with the Lord and the holy apostles and their successors as witnesses, do we permit them ever to suffer any infamy or accusation arising from these writings, or separation from their possessions.

Confession in such matters must not be compelled but voluntary, as the one who says these words bears witness: “For out of the heart come murders, adulteries, fornications, blasphemies” (Matt. 15:19), and the other things belonging to this matter.

Nor should we attend merely to what is done, but rather to the spirit in which it is done. If we began to write down all the examples of this, the days would run out before the examples did.

Hence also comes the fact that the Lord looked upon Abel’s gifts and not upon Cain’s, because he paid greater attention to the mind of the one offering than to the things offered.

Therefore the Lord says through the Prophet: “The Lord knows the thoughts of human beings” (Ps. 93:11). And through Hosea he says: “Set a trumpet to your throat, like an eagle over the house of the Lord” (Hos. 8:1), and so forth.

And the Lord says in the Gospel: “But when you pray, enter your room, and after closing the door pray to your Father” (Matt. 6:6).

For every confession made under compulsion is not faith. And the Apostle says: “With the heart one believes unto righteousness, but with the mouth confession is made unto salvation” (Rom. 10:10).

God looks more to thoughts and spontaneous intentions than to acts performed through simplicity or necessity. Confession in such matters must not be extorted, but rather freely professed. For it is the worst thing to judge anyone on the basis of suspicion or an extorted confession, since the Lord, who examines the heart, is more concerned with the heart than with the deed, and seeks pure thoughts and good intentions rather than lying lips.

Hence the Lord speaks through the prophet: “This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me” (Isa. 29:13).

I do not think there is a worse evil than Christians envying their own priests. For the Lord knows who are his. No one whom God has reserved for his own judgment can be condemned by human examination.

If everything were avenged in this world, there would be no place for divine judgments. As for the fact that such persons ought not to be accused before other judges until they have first been accused before priests or the Church’s hearers, we find that this has been observed and defined from the time of the apostles onward.

If anyone believes that he has a just complaint or legal action against a bishop or against Church officials, he should not forget the ways of his Redeemer—whose action is our instruction—but should be an outstanding follower of him who, when he was cursed, did not curse in return, but was silent like a sheep before its shearer, and while hanging on the cross interceded with the Father for his persecutors.

Such a person must not first approach primates, superiors, or other judges, but should meet privately with those whom he believes have wronged him—not once but very often—so that he may receive from them either his justice or a just explanation [Col. 0093C].

It is indeed characteristic of a good and truly Christian person to try the matter first according to all the laws of friendship and peace, before stubbornly seeking his right in court, where very often the soul’s most bitter resentment takes root.

If anyone wishes to dwell with God, who is the author of peace, he must seek peace. If he acts otherwise, let him be deprived of communion by them and by others as a despiser of the apostles, the Fathers, and the rest, concerning whom the prophet says: “They will be as though they did not exist, and the men who oppose you will perish” (Isa. 41:11).

In the offerings of the sacraments, which are offered to the Lord during the solemn celebration of Mass, the Lord’s Passion must also be mingled, so that the Passion of the one whose body and blood are consecrated may be celebrated. Thus, after superstitious opinions have been rejected, only bread and wine mixed with water are to be offered in the sacrifice [Col. 0093D].

For, as we have received from the Fathers and as reason itself teaches, neither wine alone nor water alone should be offered in the Lord’s cup, but both mixed together, because both are read to have flowed from his side during his Passion.

The Truth himself instructs us to offer the cup and bread in the sacrament when he says: “Jesus took bread, blessed it, and gave it to his disciples, saying: ‘Take and eat; for this is my body, which will be handed over for you.’”

Likewise, after he had eaten, he took the cup and gave it to his disciples, saying: “Take and drink from it, all of you, for this is the cup of my blood, which will be poured out for you for the remission of sins” [Col. 0094A] (Matt. 26:26).

Crimes and sins are wiped away when these sacrifices are offered to the Lord. Therefore his Passion, by which we were redeemed, must be commemorated in them and recited again and again. These offerings will delight and appease the Lord, and he will forgive great sins.

For nothing in the sacrifices can be greater than the body and blood of Christ. No offering is superior to this; it surpasses them all. It must be offered to the Lord with a pure conscience, received with a pure mind, and venerated by all. And just as it is superior to the others, so it must be cultivated and venerated with greater devotion.

We bless water sprinkled with salt for the people, so that all who are sprinkled with it may be sanctified and purified; and we command all priests to do this. For if the ashes of a heifer, sprinkled with blood, sanctified and cleansed the people, how much more does water sprinkled with salt, consecrated by divine prayers, sanctify and cleanse the people?

And if water was healed of barrenness when salt was sprinkled into it by the prophet Elisha, how much more does water consecrated by divine prayers remove the barrenness of human things, sanctify, cleanse, and purify the defiled, multiply other good things, turn away the plots of the devil, and defend a person from the deceits of crafty phantoms?

For if we do not doubt that the sick were healed by touching the fringe of the Savior’s garment, how much more, through the power of his sacred words, are the elements divinely consecrated, by which fragile human nature receives health of body and soul?

Instructed, therefore, by these and other teachings, attend to the vows of each person, priests of the Lord, and strive to accomplish them through divine prayers in the power of the Holy Spirit, by the ministry divinely entrusted to you.

Consecrate the elements as well—both those mentioned above and the others suitable for divine use and necessary for human infirmities. Heal the sick and diligently fulfill the other duties belonging to you. For the Savior himself, giving an example to us, said to his disciples: “In my name cast out demons, heal the weak, cure the sick, cleanse lepers, and so forth. Also lay hands on the sick, and they will be well” (Mark 16:17).

We have also received from the Fathers this teaching concerning the faith of the holy Trinity, and we intend to hand it down to you for transmission to your subjects. For the prophet Isaiah says:

> “I saw the Lord Sabaoth seated upon a lofty throne, [Col. 0094D] and Seraphim stood around him: six wings for one and six wings for the other. With two they veiled his face, with two they flew, and they cried out to one another, saying: ‘Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God Sabaoth’” (Isa. VI, 1).

If there is no Trinity, why did they say “holy” three times? Or, if there is no unity, why, under a threefold repetition, did they proclaim one God and Lord?

If there is no Trinity, why is it said in the Book of Genesis: “God spoke, God made, and God blessed”? If there is no unity, why did he say “God” three times, and not commend “gods” in the plural number?

If there is no Trinity, why is it said three times in Exodus: “Lord, Lord, compassionate and merciful”? If there is no unity, why, while saying three times “O Lord,” did he afterward say singularly [Col. 0095A] “compassionate,” and not “compassionate ones,” as he would have indicated had he been speaking of several?

If there is no Trinity, why did Abraham, seated by the oak of Mamre and encountering three, address one as “Lord,” rather than offer the salutation proper to the three whom he had seen? If there is no unity, why, when God said to Moses “the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob” three times, did he, showing unity, say, “This is my name,” and not designate them by saying, “These are our names”?

If there is no Trinity, why did David say three times:

> “May God bless us, our God; may God bless us” (Ps. LXVI, 8)?

If there is no unity, why, after naming God three times, did he say “may he bless,” and not add “may they bless”?

If there is no Trinity, why did Isaiah say again:

> “The Lord God Sabaoth, the God of Israel, who sits above the cherubim” (Isa. XXXVII, 18)?

If [Col. 0095B] there is no unity, why did he say “who sits,” and not “who sit,” using the plural?

If there is no Trinity, why is it said in the Book of Kings:

> “O Lord, almighty God, God of Israel, your words are faithful”?

If there is no unity, why is “your” said, and not rather “your [plural]”?

If there is no Trinity, why is it sung in Psalm Fifty-Eight:

> “O Lord God of hosts, God of Israel, attend to visiting all the nations”?

If there is no unity, why did he use “attend,” and not “attend, you [plural],” as would have been indicated?

If there is no Trinity, why did he say three times in the Apocalypse:

> “Holy Lord God almighty, who is and who was”?

If there is no unity, why is “who is” designated, and not “who are” in the plural?

If there is no Trinity, why is it said in Deuteronomy:

> “The Lord your God is merciful [Col. 0095C] and will hear your voice”?

If there is no unity, why did he use “will hear” and not indicate “will hear [plural]”?

If there is no Trinity, why is it said in the Book of Joshua:

> “The Lord, God of gods, is”?

If there is no unity, why did he say “is” and not employ “are,” according to the usual manner of speech?

If there is no Trinity, why did Elijah say in prayer:

> “Lord, Lord God of Israel, show that you are my God”?

If there is no unity, why did he use “show” and not “show [plural]”?

If there is no Trinity, why did Mordecai, praying, say:

> “Lord, Lord, almighty God, all things are in your power”?

If there is no unity, why did he say “in your [singular] power” and not designate “in your [plural] power”?

If there is no Trinity, why did Judith also say in prayer:

> “Lord, Lord, God of all powers, look upon my prayer”?

If there is no unity, why did he use “look” and not “look [plural]”?

[Col. 0095D] If there is no Trinity, why is it said in Jeremiah:

> “The Lord your God is the true God”?

If there is no unity, why did he say “is true,” and not rather indicate “they are true”?

If there is no Trinity, why is it written in the Apocalypse:

> “The Lord God and the spirit of the prophets sent his angel to show his servants what must happen soon”?

If there is no unity, why, after naming the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, did he say “sent,” and not introduce “they sent,” in accordance with the stated number of the three persons and names?

If there is no Trinity, why does Deuteronomy say:

> “The Lord your God is here”?

If there is no unity, why did he say “he is here,” and not designate “they are here” in the plural? [Col. 0096A]

If there is no Trinity, why is it said in the same book:

> “The Lord your God, the great and mighty God, is”?

If there is no unity, why are “great” and “mighty” not named in the plural?

If there is no Trinity, why is Tobias said to have spoken thus when he sent his son to the city of Rages with the archangel Raphael and blessed them:

> “May the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob himself fulfill his blessing in you”?

If there is no unity, why did he say “may he himself fulfill,” and not indicate “may they themselves fulfill”?

Finally, if there is no Trinity, why did the Lord send his disciples to baptize all nations in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit? If there is no unity, why did he say “in the name,” and not teach by commanding “in the names”?

If there is no Trinity, why did the apostle Paul [Col. 0096B] say:

> “From him, and through him, and in him are all things”?

If there is no unity, why did he say “from him,” and not establish “from them”?

For if you wish to recognize with complete certainty the unity of the Trinity, you can learn everything from the often-mentioned teacher of the nations, the Apostle, and follow the catholic faith while rejecting the perversity of these others. He says:

> “The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Spirit”—

the grace itself of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Thus, with the Lord’s help, you can fully understand and teach the faith of the holy Trinity.

Therefore, dearest ones, we have placed the rules of faith near the end of this letter, [Col. 0096C] so that we may persevere faithfully in its confession and, with the Lord’s help, deserve to possess the good faith.

> “Whoever wishes to be a friend of this world is constituted an enemy of God. Or do you suppose that Scripture said in vain: ‘The spirit that dwells in you desires to envy’? But he gives greater grace; therefore it says: ‘God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.’ Submit yourselves, therefore, to God; resist the devil, and he will flee from you. Draw near to the Lord, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, sinners, and purify your hearts, double-minded people. Be miserable, mourn, and weep; let your laughter be turned into mourning and your joy into sorrow. Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will exalt you. Do not speak evil of one another, my brothers, for whoever speaks evil of a brother or judges his brother speaks evil of the law and judges the law. But if you judge the law, you are not a doer [Col. 0096D] of the law but a judge. There is one lawgiver and judge, who can destroy and deliver. But who are you to judge your neighbor?” (James IV, 4–13).

> “Come now, you rich; weep, howling over the miseries that will come upon you. Your riches have rotted, and your garments have been eaten by moths. Your gold and silver have rusted, and their rust will be a testimony against you and will devour your flesh like fire. You have stored up wrath for yourselves in the last days. Behold, the wages of the laborers who harvested your lands, wages withheld by you, cry out, demanding vengeance for their retained labor; and their cry has entered the ears of the Lord Sabaoth. You have feasted upon the earth and nourished your bodies in luxury. On the day of slaughter you have brought forth and killed the just, and he did not resist you” (James V, 1–6). [Col. 0097A]

Woe, brothers, to those who trouble you. But the more greatly you are troubled, the purer and happier you will become, provided that the tribulation itself is borne patiently. Therefore Truth itself said through its own mouth:

> “Blessed are those who suffer persecution for righteousness’ sake” [Col. 0098A] (Matt. V, 10),

and elsewhere:

> “You will be blessed when people hate you, persecute you, and cast out your name as evil. Rejoice on that day and leap for joy, for your reward is great in heaven” (Matt. V, 11).

Given on the ninth day before the Kalends of August, in the consulship of Trajan and Helianus, both consuls.

## 22. The First Letter of Pope Alexander

### Concerning the causes or afflictions of priests

[Col. 0097]

[Col. 0097A] Alexander, bishop, to all the beloved brothers, the bishops established throughout the various regions.

Brothers, no one is in doubt that the good are always persecuted and afflicted by the wicked. Therefore let us humble ourselves beneath the powerful hand of God, so that he may deliver us in the time of tribulation. For just as a roaring lion goes about seeking someone to devour, so the devil never ceases to go around seeking whom among the faithful he may destroy, especially those whom he finds more ardent in the service of the Savior and more closely associated with him. [Col. 0097B] I call those “closely associated” whom he wished to be consecrated to himself and established in the order of the apostles.

They intercede for the people and consume the sins of the people, because by their prayers and offerings they blot them out and destroy them. The more worthy they are, the more readily they are heard in the necessities over which they cry out. “For,” as the blessed apostle James says, “the continual prayer of a righteous person is very powerful” (James V, 16).

Whoever persecutes you persecutes the one whose embassy you perform. For just as the Son of God himself was mediator between God and human beings, so you have been appointed in his place in the Church, to serve as ambassadors between the Lord and humanity. Whoever impedes your embassy overturns the progress not of one person but of many. And just as he harms many, so he must be rebuked by many and [Col. 0097C] excluded from the fellowship of the good. Since he impedes God’s cause and disturbs the order of the Church, let him therefore be barred from the thresholds of the Church.

Such a person must also be avoided by human beings and not received into the communion of the faithful until he has made satisfaction. For it was formerly decreed that whoever disturbs the order of the Church should be barred from its thresholds, so that he who turns away their goods may not communicate with the faithful.

Therefore, if you have love for one another and are united in mind, you will easily be able to overcome such people. But if—which God forbid—you are divided and begin to gnaw at one another with a dog’s tooth, you will not only fail to overcome them; you will also harm yourselves, be overcome by them, and perhaps perish innocently. [Col. 0097D]

Whoever belongs to your college yet withdraws himself from your assistance will be shown to be a schismatic rather than a priest. “Behold,” says the prophet, “how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together in unity” (Ps. CXXXII, 1).

Those do not dwell together in unity who withdraw from the support of their brothers or, worse still, prepare ambushes or set traps for their brothers. Concerning such people and their kind, the Lord speaks through the prophet Hosea, saying:

> “Because of you the land will mourn, and everyone who dwells in it will grow weak, [Col. 0098A] together with the beasts of the field and the birds of the sky; even the fish of the sea will be gathered up. Yet let no one judge, and let no man be reproved, for your people are like those who contradict the priest. You will stumble today, and the prophet will also stumble with you. At night I made your mother silent. My people became silent because they had no knowledge. Because you rejected knowledge, I will reject you, so that you may not serve as priest to me. Since you forgot the law of your God, I too will forget your children. According to the multitude [Col. 0098B] of them, so they sinned against me; I will change their glory into disgrace. They eat the sins of my people and lift up their souls toward their iniquity. It will be as with the people, so with the priest; I will visit his ways upon him and repay his thoughts to him. They will eat and not be satisfied; they committed fornication and did not cease, because they abandoned the Lord by failing to keep watch” (Hos. IV, 3).

Beware of these things, brothers, and hasten always to do what is good, because, as the Lord says, “by this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another.” It is unquestionably good, and desirable to all who fear God, to restrain dissensions and quarrels, to assist one’s brothers, [Col. 0098C] and not to envy one another but to help one another.

Therefore we who desire both to be called and to be disciples of the Lord must carry Christ’s cross and suffer with our brothers, and not prepare any ambushes or pits for them, because whoever prepares a pit for his brothers deserves the same treatment.

Do not err, brothers, for God is not mocked. For this reason the Lord entrusted his Church to you: so that you might labor for all and not neglect to bring aid to all who are oppressed. Therefore the Lord speaks through the prophet, saying:

> “Thus says the Lord: Judge judgment in the morning and rescue the oppressed by force from the hand of the slanderer, lest my indignation go forth like fire, and be kindled, with no one to extinguish it” (Jer. XXI, 12).

[Col. 0098D] Therefore, you who have been placed by the Lord upon the highest watchtower must watch over and restrain those who stir up seditions and scandals against their brothers, lest you perish together with them.

Greet all who labor rightly in the Gospel of Christ and govern his ship justly, lest those dwelling in it be submerged or suffocated. The entire apostolic Church greets you in the Lord. Amen.

Given on the seventh day before the Kalends of November, in the consulship of Trajan and Helianus, both consuls.

## The Second Letter of Pope Alexander

### That slander and unjust accusations are to be avoided

[Col. 0099]

[Col. 0099] Alexander, bishop, to all who exercise the divine priesthood: may peace and mercy be multiplied, and may wisdom [Col. 0099A] and good will increase and bear fruit in all things in the Lord.

Brothers most beloved, by the grace of God we are what we are. Therefore we must take care, and strive with great determination, lest we be found empty in that grace, but, with the same grace cooperating with us, bring the Lord an abundant harvest. This cannot happen otherwise than by pursuing wisdom, meditating upon its precepts through readings and hymns, and, with its assistance, striving to fulfill them through prayer and vigilance, and to accomplish his will insofar as he himself grants us strength.

The Lord has not given us this same grace to neglect it, but has granted it to be exercised faithfully. Love must exist and be seen in us without pretense, because everyone who hates his brother is a murderer. [Col. 0099B] Whoever loves him remains in God, and God in him. Therefore the Apostle says:

> “Do not judge one another, brothers, but judge this rather: that you do not place a stumbling-block or a scandal before your brother.”

And the Lord says:

> “What you do not wish to be done to you, do not do to another.”

And elsewhere:

> “By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another.”

Solomon also says:

> “A saving sacrifice is to attend to the commandments and depart from all iniquity.”

For the greatest iniquity is to slander and accuse one’s brothers. Hence it is written:

> “Everyone who slanders his brother is a murderer.”

Every murderer has no share or inheritance in the kingdom of God. And elsewhere:

> “Beware, most beloved brothers, lest you become participants—which God forbid—in their evils.”

Do not merely guard yourselves from such people; [Col. 0099C] teach others also to beware of them and to turn away from them. Concerning them the Lord says through the prophet Micah:

> “Woe to those who devise what is useless and work evil upon their beds. In the morning light they do it, because their hand is against God. They coveted fields and seized them by violence; they robbed houses and oppressed a man and his house, a man and his inheritance. Therefore the Lord says this: Behold, I am devising evil against this family, from which you will not remove your necks, and you will not walk proudly, for the time is very evil. On that day a proverb will be taken up against you, and a song will be sung with sweetness, saying: ‘We have been utterly devastated by devastation; the portion of my people [Col. 0100] has been changed. How will he depart from me, when the one who devours your regions returns?’ Therefore [Col. 0100A] there will be no one casting a measuring-line for you by lot in the assembly of the Lord, O Israel. Do not speak, speaking. No drop will fall upon these; confusion will not seize them, says the Lord of Jacob. Has the spirit of the Lord been shortened, or are such his thoughts? Are not my words good toward the one who walks rightly? But, on the contrary, my people rose up as an enemy: you stripped the cloak from above the garment and turned those who passed by innocently toward war.”

And, on the other hand, concerning those who are accused or afflicted, the Lord speaks through the prophet Nahum, comforting them:

> “He is a stronghold in the day of tribulation, and he knows those who hope in him. In the passing flood he will bring the end of its place, and darkness will pursue his enemies. What are you devising against the Lord? [Col. 0100B] He himself will establish the stronghold. Affliction will not rise up twice. For just as thorns embrace one another, so, while they feast together as drinkers, they will be consumed like straw full of dryness. From you will go forth one who devises evil against the Lord, considering treachery in his mind. Thus says the Lord: Though they be complete, and likewise many, even so they will be shorn and pass away. I afflicted you, but I will not afflict you any longer.”

It is easy to deceive a human being by a word, but not God. The wise person is not one who harms, nor will the person of a malicious tongue direct himself toward evil upon the earth; but the faithful person desires no evil.

Faith is foreign to an evil and perverse disposition. For the Apostle says concerning the ignorance of unbelievers:

> “For if they had known, they would never have crucified the Lord of glory.”

They crucify the Lord who persecute him [Col. 0100C] in his priests, because *crux* (“cross”) is said from *cruciatus* (“torment”). Great indeed is the sacred burden borne by one who suffers with another. Nevertheless:

> “Blessed are those who suffer persecution for righteousness’ sake.”

Behold, the apostle Jude says:

> “The Lord will come with his thousands to execute judgment, to destroy all the ungodly, and to convict all flesh concerning all their ungodliness.”

These things, brothers, are greatly to be feared and carefully weighed, lest, when each person comes to judgment, he receive punishment with the ungodly rather than glory with the righteous. May the merciful Lord grant this—he who lives and reigns forever and ever.

Given on the Kalends of May, in the consulship of Helianus and Vetus, both consuls.

## The Decrees of Pope Sixtus I Begin

*(In the year of the Lord 129, during the time of Hadrian.)*

[Col. 0099]

[Col. 0099D] Sixtus, archbishop of the Roman Church, to all beloved brothers in God the Father and in our Lord Jesus Christ, in the love of our Lord Jesus Christ: greetings.

Dearest ones, act faithfully in all things, so that you may be found faithful and not unfaithful. Do not imitate evil, but do what is good, because whoever is from God does good, while whoever does evil is not from God but from the devil. [Col. 0100D]

You must hold the right faith, so that you may not dissent from apostolic teaching. We have shown that one true God, the Father and the Son, was preached by the prophets and apostles; and from them we also believe that the Holy Spirit is not separated. The prophet Isaiah says:

> “I am God, and there is no other besides me. I swear by myself, because truth has gone forth from my mouth; and my word does not turn back, [Col. 0101A] because every knee will bow to me, and every tongue will confess through the Lord, saying: ‘Justice and glory will come to him.’”

And so that you may understand that the Father and the Son were together in this testimony, hear the apostle Paul saying:

> “So that at the name of Jesus,” he says, “every knee should bow, of those in heaven, on earth, and under the earth, and every tongue confess that the Lord Jesus Christ is in the glory of God the almighty Father.”

But if, according to some, the Son is lesser than his Father, then the glory of the Father in the Son has also been diminished [23]. And where is what Scripture says in Solomon:

> “For just as,” he says, “you were magnified in their sight in us, so you will be magnified in our sight in them, that they may know you as we also have known you, because there is no God besides you, O Lord”?

Attend carefully and [Col. 0101B] recognize that it is the Son who will be magnified in judgment, when he comes to judge the living and the dead.

Isaiah likewise says:

> “Hear, O house of Jacob, and the remnant of the house of Israel, you who come forth from the womb and are instructed from childhood to old age. From the beginning I am, and until you grow old I am. I made you, and I sustain you; I will forgive; I will receive,” says the Lord. [Col. 0101B]

And again:

> “I am the Lord God; besides me there is no other God, announcing the last things before they happen, and immediately they were accomplished.”

Elsewhere:

> “Hear me, Jacob and Israel, because I made you. I am the Lord your God, and there is no other besides me.”

And there:

> “I am the Lord your God, the first, and I am the last; and in the things that are to come, in the last days, I am. I am the God who created you, who helped you, and who strengthened you with my right hand.”

And, assigning the unity of the Father and [Col. 0101C] the Son, he says:

> “You are my witnesses, says the Lord God, and my servant whom I chose, so that you may know and believe that I am, and before me there was no other God, and after me there will not be.”

Let those who do not think soundly choose one of two alternatives: either let them confess the Father and the Son to be one God, or, if they contend that the Father alone is God, then our Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God, will not be God for them, because it is written:

> “Before me there was no other God, and after me there will not be.”

If, according to such people, this is so, why does the Apostle preach such things and identify the same Son as God, blessed above all?

> “Whose are the fathers,” he says, “and from them is Christ according to the flesh, who is God over all, blessed forever.”

[Col. 0101D] Isaiah also says:

> “The Lord God of Israel, who delivered him from Egypt. I am the first, and I am after these things, and besides me there is no God like me, who shall stand, call, and make ready for me, from the time when I made a human being in the world.”

Elsewhere:

> “In you is God, and we did not know it; and there is no other God besides you. For you are God, and we did not know it, God of Israel, Savior.”

Are the Father and the Son not one God? Who is this God in whom God is said to be, while the prophet repeatedly declares that there is no other God?

And Baruch:

> “This is our God,” he says, “and no other will be compared with him, who discovered every way of knowledge and gave it to Jacob his servant and to Israel his beloved. After this he appeared on earth and lived among human beings.”

And in Solomon it is found:

> [Col. 0102A] “Have mercy on us, God of all, and show us the light of your mercy; send your fear upon the nations that have not sought you, so that they may know that there is no other God except you.”

Elsewhere:

> “Lord God of Israel, there is none like you in heaven above or on earth below.”

And in Psalm Seventeen:

> “For who is God besides the Lord, or who is God besides our God?”

And in Genesis:

> “The Lord rained fire and sulfur from the Lord upon Sodom and Gomorrah and overthrew those cities.”

If the Father alone is God, who rained fire and sulfur upon the aforesaid cities to overthrow them? I ask you to answer.

And in Deuteronomy:

> “The Lord alone led them, and there was no foreign god with them.”

[Col. 0102B] The apostle Paul says:

> “One God who justifies circumcision by faith and uncircumcision through faith.”

And to the Corinthians:

> “God was in Christ, reconciling the world to himself.”

And again:

> “There is no God except one.”

And to the Galatians:

> “A mediator, however, is not of one; but God is one.”

And, demonstrating the unity of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, he confirms it by writing to the Ephesians:

> “Bearing with one another in love, carefully preserve the unity of the spirit in the bond of peace: one body and one spirit, just as you were called in one hope of your calling; one God, one faith, one baptism, one God” (Eph. IV, 2).

If those who do not think soundly are willing to receive the unity of the faith with a simple heart, then from this testimony they can learn together, in one Spirit, the unity of the Father and the Son.

The Father, therefore, as was established above, cannot be entirely read or proved in the divine writings as specifically designated *ingenitus*, “unbegotten.” But because Christian faith requires this, the one who is unbegotten is believed without any doubt; nevertheless, according to the sequence of the Scriptures, he is shown to be one with the Son begotten from him.

[Col. 0102C] For the rest, on account of the attacks of wicked people, it has seemed good that, when the Lord’s ministers are accused, the person, faith, life, and conduct of those making the accusation should first be examined in detail. For faith must precede all a person’s actions: whoever is uncertain in faith is unfaithful. Those who do not know the faith of truth and do not lead a life of right conduct must not be believed at all. Such people readily and indiscriminately tear apart and accuse those who live rightly and piously. Therefore their suspicion must first be examined and corrected, and credence must not be given to accusers who are suspect or who come from the household of enemies. [Col. 0102D]

For there were some who initially appeared to be from among us, but they were not from among us. If they had been from among us, they would certainly have remained with us and would not have disturbed the brothers. “For,” as the prophet says,

> “They sharpened their tongues like serpents; the venom of asps is under their lips” (Ps. CXXXIX, 4).

Therefore such people must be rejected if they appear incorrigible, and avoided lest they deceive those who serve the Lord.

Stand, then, dearest ones, beside the ways, watching and asking about the ancient paths of the Lord. See which is the good and straight way of the Lord, walk in it, and you will find rest for your souls.

Given on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of May, under Hadrian and Verus.

## Another Letter of Pope Sixtus

[Col. 0103]

[Col. 0103A] Sixtus, bishop of the universal apostolic Church, to all bishops: greetings in the Lord.

Let your wisdom know, dearest brothers, that we, together with the other bishops and the other priests of the Lord, have decreed in this holy apostolic See that sacred vessels may be handled only by those consecrated and devoted to the Lord. It is wholly unworthy that any sacred vessels of the Lord should serve human uses or be handled by men other than those who serve and are devoted to the Lord.

Let the angry Lord not inflict a plague upon his people because of such presumptions, so that even those who have not sinned may suffer evil or perish, for the righteous very often perishes on account of the wicked.

Take care, brothers, that you do not henceforth permit such things to be done by men in the churches, lest the flock redeemed by the precious [Col. 0103B] blood of Christ fall—which God forbid—into a precipice. Therefore take up the armor of God, so that you may be able to resist those who contradict the truth, and put on the breastplate of righteousness, with your feet shod in readiness for the Gospel of peace.

If any of you is brought before a tribunal in some adversity, let him freely appeal to this holy and apostolic See and have recourse to it as to the head, lest an innocent person be condemned or his Church suffer harm. But if it is necessary for him to appeal to it and he has not dared to do so, yet is summoned by this holy See, let him not refuse to come. As soon as he has been notified, let him hasten to come, prudently arrange the matters for which he has been summoned, and, if anything needs to be corrected, correct it with those whom he first finds here. [Col. 0103C]

Nevertheless, let him not return to his Church before he has been fully instructed and cleared by apostolic letters or *formatae*—letters of the prescribed form—if there is any matter requiring this. After he has returned home, let his neighbors know how his case and the cases of others were examined here, so that he may be able to report and proclaim it to everyone without any ambiguity. [Col. 0104A]

For bishops have been commanded to be protected, defended, and delivered by this holy See and by the holy apostles, so that, just as they were first established by the Lord through the apostles’ ordering, so in future times they may always be free from every perversity through the protection of this holy See, to whose judgment they have entrusted their cases and decisions. Therefore those are condemned who act toward their brothers otherwise than they know to be pleasing to the rulers of this See.

Having considered these matters in this way and decreed them with the other bishops, as those who bear care for all, we decree, on account of the dignity of our own See, that no bishop may presume to excommunicate or judge another bishop who has been stripped of his possessions or expelled from his see. There is no privilege by which one already stripped may be stripped again.

[Col. 0104B] If anyone presumes to act otherwise, let him know that the censure of this See, together with all its members, will come upon him; and as he has acted, so will he receive. If well, well; if gravely, gravely; if most wickedly, most wickedly, because the laborer is worthy of his wage.

Brothers, we desire to destroy no one; but the one who turns away from what has been piously considered destroys himself, as does the one who willingly violates the decrees of the apostles and of this holy See.

But now, brothers, we commend you all to God and to the word of his grace, which can perfect and give an inheritance with all the saints. May the God of peace and consolation grant you to think the same thing toward one another, so that you may assist one another and not be divided. Thus, united in mind, with one mouth and one heart, may we honor him in harmony and in the consolation of the brothers—him who is powerful to strengthen us [Col. 0104C] according to his Gospel, in accordance with the revelation of the eternal mystery, throughout perpetual ages, in which the gifts of future joys are to be bestowed upon you.

Given on the ninth day before the Kalends of April, in the consulship of Hadrian and Verus, both consuls.

## The Decrees of Pope Telesphorus Begin

### Concerning the seven-week fast before Easter, the celebration of Mass on the holy night of the Nativity of the Lord, the times at which Masses are to be celebrated on other days, and the defense of bishops

*(In the year of the Lord 131, during the reign of the emperor Antoninus Pius.)*

[Col. 0103]

[Col. 0103C] Telesphorus, archbishop of the city of Rome, to his dearest brothers and beloved bishops: greetings in the Lord.

We believe that your holy faith is founded upon the apostles’ teaching, and that you hold it and explain it to all peoples—faith which in no respect departs from the decrees of the apostles and their successors, through whom it is right that the others should be instructed. Therefore know from us and from all the bishops gathered into this holy and apostolic See that it has been decreed that, for seven full weeks before holy [Col. 0104C] Easter, all clerics called into the Lord’s portion [Col. 0104D] shall abstain from meat; for just as the life of clerics ought to be distinct from the conduct of laypeople, so there ought also to be a distinction in fasting. And just as laypeople and secular persons do not wish to receive clerics in their accusations and denunciations, so clerics ought not to receive laypeople in their own accusations; for in all things the life and conduct of clerics and secular laypeople ought always to be distinct and separate.

And just as these men are more devoted to divine worship and are called the household of the Lord [Col. 0105A] the Savior, so in morals, conduct, and holiness they ought to be distinguished. Therefore, throughout these seven weeks, let all clerics fast from meat and delicacies, and strive day and night to cling to the Lord through hymns, vigils, and prayers.

On the holy night of the birth of the Lord the Savior, let them celebrate Masses and solemnly sing the angelic hymn in them, since on that same night the birth was announced by an angel to the shepherds, as the Truth itself bears witness, saying:

“Now there were shepherds in that region, keeping watch and guarding the watches of the night over their flock. And behold, an angel of the Lord stood beside them, and they were afraid with great fear. And the angel said to them: ‘Do not be afraid, for behold, I announce to you great joy, which will be for all the people, because today a Savior has been born for you, who is [Col. 0105B] Christ the Lord, in the city of David. And this will be the sign for you: you will find an infant wrapped in swaddling clothes and lying in a manger.’ And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly army, praising the Lord and saying: ‘Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to people of good will’ (Luke II, 8–14).”

Moreover:

“The wicked watches the just man and seeks to kill 24 him. The Lord will not abandon him into his hands, nor will he condemn him when judgment is rendered against him. Wait for the Lord and keep his way, and he will exalt you so that you may possess the land; when the wicked perish, you will see it. I saw the wicked man, vigorous and exceedingly strong, like a native tree flourishing, and I passed by, and behold, he was no more; I sought him, and he was not found. Keep innocence and observe what is right, because in [Col. 0105C] the end there will be peace for the man; but transgressors will perish together, and the last remnant of the wicked will perish. But the salvation of the just is from the Lord, their strength in the time of tribulation. The Lord will help them, save them, and rescue them from the wicked; he will save them, because they have taken refuge in him.”

And elsewhere:

“Why do you boast in wickedness, mighty man? The mercy of God endures all day. Your tongue devised plots like a sharpened razor, practicing deceit. You loved wickedness more than goodness, falsehood more than speaking righteousness. You loved every devouring word, deceitful tongue. But God will destroy you forever; he will terrify you and tear you out of your tent, and uproot you from the land of the living. The just will see and fear, and they will laugh at him. Behold the man who did not set his strength in [Col. 0105D] God, but trusted in the multitude of his riches and grew strong in his plots. But I am like a flourishing olive tree in the house of God; I have trusted in the mercy of God forever and ever. I will give thanks to you forever, because you have acted, and I will await your name, because it is good in the presence of your mercies.”

At other times, Masses are by no means to be celebrated before the third hour of the day, because it was at that same hour that the Lord was crucified and because the Holy Spirit is read to have descended upon the apostles. The bishops, however, are to celebrate and solemnly recite this same angelic hymn at the appropriate time and place during the solemn celebrations of Mass.

[Col. 0106A] Those who with their own mouths consecrate the Lord’s body are to be obeyed and feared by all, and must not be torn apart or disparaged. For those from whom the people of the Lord desire to receive blessing, salvation, and instruction must in no way be accused by them, nor may the crowd be received against them in accusation. The people are to be taught and corrected by them, not they by the people, for the disciple is not above the teacher.

Therefore, the bishops and other priests of the Lord, to whom the Lord’s people have been entrusted, cannot rightly correct the people if they themselves know that they are being harassed by the snare of deceit. Hence it is right that all teachers of the law throughout the world should think on the things that are of the law, and that no one should defile the priests of the Lord with his lips or by any other contrivance. While such people plan or desire to defile them, they rather defile and wound themselves.

Therefore, whoever accuses the priests whom God has appointed accuses God’s ordinance, and desires their condemnation. All the faithful ought to guard themselves from such people, because not only those who commit an act but also those who consent to its perpetrators are guilty.

For Christ, the Son of God, our Lord, granting the human race full salvation, says concerning us:

“Whoever receives you receives me, and whoever despises you despises me” (Matthew X, 40; Luke X, 16).

If, then, the Lord is received or rejected in them, undoubtedly those who receive or reject them are his. And who are you, that you judge another’s servant? Undoubtedly, you are transgressors of the law of God, of the apostles, and of the prophets—not only of these laws, but also of human laws. [Col. 0106C] For all laws, both divine and human, forbid judging another’s servant.

What do you suppose will become of you when the transgressors and tramplers of God’s law are condemned? Certainly you too will be condemned, because you have set aside God’s commandment and fulfilled your own will. For just as those who fulfill and keep God’s commandment are worthy of life, so those who set it aside and treat it as worthless are guilty and entirely worthy of death.

It is written in the apostolic ordinances that no one should tear apart another’s life or defile his mouth with another’s evil. As for accusers and accusations, which the laws of the world do not admit, we also remove them, and we decree that no credence at all is to be given to an accuser who, in the absence of his opponent, presents a case before a just examination of both parties. Nor are those who are unqualified to be admitted as accusers; and we judge all who take up arms against fathers to be infamous.

For all fathers are to be revered, not rejected or plotted against. Those who live with enemies, or who are held under suspicion, are by no means to be admitted, because their hostility tears apart even the innocent. Our fathers established this strongest of walls, and we have established it with them against our persecutors, so that their schemes may be driven away by this remedy and you may deserve to serve your Savior more securely and more holily.

Concerning such plotters and accusers of his servants the Lord speaks through the prophet, saying:

“You sent your mouth toward wickedness, and your tongue fashioned deceit. Sitting against your brother, you spoke, and against the son of your mother you devised reproach. You have done these things, and I was silent. You thought that I would become like you? I will rebuke you and set the matter before your eyes. Understand this, you who forget the Lord, lest he seize you and there be no one to deliver.”

Those who are weak in this undertaking must be marked and driven away from such people. For such men are members of the devil, who flies above and below seeking what he may kill, whom he may separate, and whom he may devour. Therefore we must keep watch and be armed with heavenly weapons, lest we fall into his fetters or be ensnared in his pits.

In such cases, care must especially be taken that, without the uproar of disputes, charity may be preserved [Col. 0107B] and truth defended, [Col. 0108A] and that the innocent and the ministers of the Lord may be delivered unharmed. Concerning good brothers who keep the law of the Lord, help, do no harm, but support others, the Lord says through the prophet:

“I have not sat with men of vanity, and I will not enter with the proud. I have hated the assembly of the wicked, and I will not sit with the impious. I will wash my hands in innocence and go around your altar, Lord, that I may proclaim your praise with a clear voice and recount all your wonders. Lord, I have loved the dwelling of your house and the place of the tabernacle of your glory. Do not place my soul with sinners, nor my life with men of blood, in whose hands is crime and whose right hand is filled with gifts. But I will walk in my innocence; redeem me and have mercy on me. My foot has stood on the right path; in the churches I will bless the Lord.”

Let these judgments of charity, then, agree with all the priests of God; in them we judge that you have remained fixed and firm. May God keep you unharmed, dearest sons. Given on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of March, in the consulship of Antoninus and Marcus, for the fourth time.

## The Decrees of Pope Hyginus Begin

Concerning the faith and other matters. (In the year of the Lord 143, during the reign of the emperor Antoninus Pius.)

[Col. 0107]

[Col. 0107C] Hyginus, bishop of Rome, the nurturing city, in the name of Christ, to all dwelling in apostolic faith and teaching: greetings.

Dearest ones, God sent his Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and, because of sin, condemned sin in the flesh, so that the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled. The Son was not sent by the Father according to divinity alone, but according to the flesh, which in his mercy and piety he did not disdain to assume for us.

For that the same Son sent himself, having emptied himself of the power of his majesty, the Apostle bears witness and says:

“He emptied himself, taking the form of a servant; he humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death, even death on a cross” (Philippians II, 7–8).

And Isaiah:

“Not an ambassador, nor an angel, but God himself will come and save [Col. 0107D] us.”

And in the same place:

“I appeared openly to those who did not seek me.”

And Jeremiah:

“I abandoned my house, I left my inheritance; I came and became a reproach to them.”

And in Micah:

“Behold, the Lord will come, and the mountains will be shaken beneath him.”

And in Zechariah:

“Rejoice and exult, daughter of Zion, because behold, I am coming and I will dwell in your midst, says the Lord.”

And the Apostle to Timothy:

“This saying is trustworthy and worthy of complete acceptance: Christ Jesus came into this world to save sinners.”

And Malachi:

“Behold, suddenly the Lord whom you seek will come to his temple, and the angel of the covenant whom you desire.”

In the Gospel:

“I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”

And in the same place:

“What have we to do with you, Jesus, Son of God? Have you come before the time to destroy us?” The Son of Man has come to save and seek what had perished.

And in the same place:

“I have come so that they may have life, and have it more abundantly.”

And again:

“No one has ascended into heaven except the one who descended from heaven, the Son of Man who is in heaven.”

In such numerous and such great testimonies, in which the Son of God testified that he had come of his own accord, could anyone say that he came from another and not from himself? It is manifest that he who graciously assumed our flesh came voluntarily and was not sent by another. For he who remains in the Father and is present everywhere by his own power had no place to which he could be sent by the Father, since no part of heaven or earth is excluded from the Father’s sight. According to you, then, where would the Son be sent by the Father?

And Paul says:

“Be renewed in the spirit of your mind, and put on the new man, who has been created according to God in righteousness and the holiness of truth.”

And to the Hebrews:

“For in that which he himself suffered and was tempted, he is able to assist those who are tempted.”

Hence you are always participants in the heavenly calling. Consider the Apostle and high priest of our confession, Jesus, faithful to the one who appointed him.

And to the Colossians:

“But now put away all these things: anger, indignation, malice, blasphemy, and let no shameful word proceed from your mouth. Do not lie to one another. Strip off the old man with his practices, and put on the new man, who is renewed in knowledge according to the image of the one who created him.”

Could the one who by the power of his own authority created and fashioned the whole creation, visible and invisible, have created or been able to make himself either before or afterward—which it is impious to say?

And the Lord says in the Gospel:

“I and the Father are one.”

And again:

“Whoever sees me sees the Father also.”

And again:

“Whoever hates me hates my Father also.”

And again:

“That all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father.”

And again:

“That they may be one in us, just as we are one. You in me, and I in them.”

And again:

“All that is mine is yours.”

And again:

“I am in the Father, and the Father is in me.”

And again:

“The Father, remaining in me, does these works.”

And John the evangelist says:

“In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God” (John I, 1).

And again, in his letter to the Parthians:

“There are three who bear witness on earth: water, blood, and flesh; these three are in us. And there are three who bear witness in heaven: the Father, the Word, and the Spirit, and these three are one.”

Therefore, since the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are one in the nature of divinity, we do not believe that the Father preceded the Son at any time, so that he might be greater than the Son, nor that the Son was born afterward, so that he might be inferior to the Father in divinity.

Moreover, brothers, without prejudice in all things to the privilege of the Roman Church, no metropolitan may hear the cases of any persons without the attendance of all the other bishops of his province; for proceedings conducted otherwise than in the presence of all of them will be invalid, and if he does so, he is to be restrained by the brothers.

[Col. 0110A] Let accusations against persons of rank not be made through others, but only by those who bring the charges themselves—provided that they appear worthy and irreproachable, and have demonstrated through public records that they are free from every suspicion and enmity 25 and lead an irreproachable life and conduct.
