The intention of your religious purpose, which has been made known to us and burns devoutly in Christ, and the report of your most sincere faith that has reached us and been approved, require us to use you as a fellow minister in the administration of the divine word, for which, by God’s grace, we are responsible.

We have learned that from childhood you studied the sacred writings, and that, as your natural gifts advanced, you extended them toward the increase of the talent entrusted from heaven, directing the grace of your kinship with the heavenly oracle, through the insight of divine love, into the labor of saving preaching, so that you might make the ministry of faith known to unbelieving peoples with persistent effort.

We rejoice in your faith and wish to be helpers of the grace granted to you. Therefore, because you have brought the devout purpose of these efforts as far as the apostolic see’s prudent consideration, it has seemed advisable that, as a member seeking the head from its own body, you should prove the movement of your mind; humbly submitting to the head’s judgment, hastening along the right path under its direction, you may become a full part of the solidity of the joined structure.

Therefore, in the name of the indivisible Trinity, through the unshakable authority of blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, whose teaching ministry we administer and whose sacred see we govern, we establish and command the discipline of religion: in the word of God’s grace—the saving fire which the Lord came to cast upon the earth (Luke 12:49)—strive, as God supports you, to proceed from the Jews to whatever peoples are held by the error of unbelief.

By proclaiming the spirit of truth, love, and sobriety, and by persuading them of the truth, set forth the mystery of the kingdom of God through the proclamation of the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, and pour it into the minds of the unlearned in a manner consistent with both Testaments.

Finally, concerning the discipline of the sacrament which you should strive to maintain for those who are to believe with God going before them, we wish you to pay attention, for the sake of your instruction, to the formula of the offices of our holy apostolic see already set forth above.

Whatever you perceive to be lacking for the work you have undertaken, take care to report to us as you are able.

Farewell.

Given on the Ides of May, while the most devout lord Augustus Leo, crowned by God, the great emperor, was reigning, in the third year of his reign, in the second indiction.

## Another letter of the same to bishops, presbyters or deacons, and all Christians

**Gregory, servant of the servants of God, to all most reverend and most holy brother bishops, religious men, presbyters or deacons, glorious commanders, magnificent castaldi, counts, and all Christians who fear God.**

Because we bear an excessive concern for the watch entrusted to us, we have learned that certain peoples in the regions of Germany, or on the eastern side of the River Rhine, are wandering in the shadow of death at the urging of the ancient enemy and, as though under the name of Christian religion, serving the worship of idols. Others, who do not yet possess knowledge of God and have not been washed in the water of holy baptism, are pagans who, like brute animals, do not acknowledge their Maker.

Therefore, for the illumination of both groups, we have taken care to send among those peoples the bearer of this letter, our most reverend brother Boniface, bishop, to preach the word of the true faith. By preaching, he is to provide the way of eternal life; and if he should discover anyone, anywhere, who has departed from the path of the true faith or whom he finds led astray by diabolical cunning, he is to correct them and, by his instruction, bring them back to the harbor of salvation. He is to form them according to the teaching of this apostolic see and establish them to remain in the same Catholic faith.

We therefore exhort you, for love of our Lord Jesus Christ and reverence for his apostles, to support him in all his efforts with your whole strength and to receive him in the name of Jesus Christ, as it is written concerning his disciples: “Whoever receives you receives me” (Matthew 10:40).

Moreover, provide what is necessary for his journey, supplying companions, food and drink, and whatever else he may need, so that, through a common labor and shared willingness, the work of piety and the task of salvation entrusted to him may be completed with God’s help, and so that you may deserve to receive the rewards of your labor and have the merit of the conversion of those who have gone astray credited to you in heaven.

Therefore, if anyone gives consent or assistance to this servant of God, sent by the apostolic and Catholic Church of God for the illumination of the peoples, may he deserve, through the prayers of the princes of the apostles, fellowship with the saints and martyrs of Jesus Christ.

But if anyone—which we do not desire—attempts by opposition to impede his labor or proves hostile to the ministry entrusted to him, let him be struck, by divine judgment, with the bond of anathema, together with those who enter upon the same labor after him, and let him be subject to perpetual damnation.

Farewell.

Given on the Kalends of December, while the most devout lord Augustus Leo, crowned by God, the great emperor, was reigning, in the seventh year, and while Constantine, his son, the great emperor, was likewise in the fourth year, in the sixth indiction.

## Another letter of Pope Gregory to the entire clergy and people of Thuringia

**Gregory, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the clergy, order, and people residing in Thuringia, his most beloved sons in the Lord: greetings.**

We have brought no delay to your worthy desires. We have ordained for you our brother and fellow bishop Boniface as bishop, and we have instructed him never to presume illicit ordinations; not to permit a bigamist, or a man who has not taken a virgin as wife [the printed text reads *virgiginem*], nor an illiterate man, nor anyone disabled in any part of his body, nor anyone marked as a penitent, a curial, or subject to any condition, to approach the sacred orders.

If he should happen to find any such men, he must not dare to promote them. He must in no way receive Africans [*Afros*] who present themselves indiscriminately for ecclesiastical orders, because some of them have been found to be Manichaeans and some repeatedly rebaptized.

He should strive not to diminish but to increase the ministries and adornment of the church, and whatever belongs to its patrimony. From the church’s revenues or the offerings of the faithful, he should make four portions: one he should retain for himself; a second he should distribute to the clergy in proportion to their diligent service; a third he should reserve for the poor and strangers; and a fourth he should know to be reserved for ecclesiastical buildings. For these he will have to render an account at the divine judgment.

He should know that the ordinations of presbyters and deacons are to be celebrated only during the fasts of the fourth, seventh, and tenth months, as well as at the beginning of Lent, and in the middle of the evening of Saturday.

The sacrament of holy baptism, however, is to be administered only at the feast of Easter and at Pentecost, except to those who, when death is pressing, must be aided by such remedies lest they perish eternally.

We ought therefore to obey with devoted hearts whoever observes the commands of our see, so that the body of the Church may become irreproachable and pleasing through our Lord, who lives and reigns with God the almighty Father and the Holy Spirit throughout all ages of ages.

May God keep you safe, most beloved sons.

Given on the Kalends of December, while the most devout lord Augustus Leo, crowned by God, the great emperor, was reigning, in the seventh year, and while Constantine, his son, the great emperor, was likewise in the fourth year, in the sixth indiction.

## Another letter of Pope Gregory to the clergy and people of Thuringia

**To the magnificent men and sons Asuelo, Guodelano, Mulereo, Gunthareo, Alvaldo, and to all the Christian faithful of Thuringia beloved by God: Pope Gregory.**

Recognizing the magnificent steadfastness of your faith in Christ that has been reported to us—that when pagans compelled you to worship idols, you answered with faith that you preferred to die happily rather than violate in any way the faith once received in Christ—we have been filled with exceeding joy and offer due thanks to our God and to the Redeemer, the giver of all good things.

With his grace accompanying you, we desire that you advance toward better and higher things and, to confirm the purpose of your faith, adhere with devout minds to the holy apostolic see. Whenever the work of sacred religion requires it, seek assistance from that holy apostolic see, the spiritual mother of all the faithful, just as sons who are co-heirs of a kingdom should seek it from their royal parent.

Through the ministry of our dearest brother Boniface, whom we have consecrated bishop and sent to you in the lot of preaching, instructed in apostolic teachings, we wish and urge you in all things to consent to him obediently, for the completion of your salvation in the Lord.

## Another letter of Pope Gregory to the Thuringians

**Gregory, servant of the servants of God, to the entire people of the Thuringians.**

The Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God, true God, descended from heaven and became human for us. He deigned to suffer and be crucified, was buried, rose from the dead on the third day, and ascended into heaven. He also said to his disciples, the holy apostles: “Go, teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit” (Matthew 28:19). For he promised eternal life to those who believe in him (John 3:36).

Because we desire you to rejoice with us forever, where there is no end, no tribulation, and no bitterness, but everlasting glory, we have therefore sent our most holy brother Boniface, the bishop, to you, so that he may baptize you, teach you the faith of Christ, and lead you back from error to the way of salvation, so that you may have salvation and eternal life.

Obey him in everything, honor him as your father, and incline your hearts to his teaching, because we did not send him to you to seek any temporal profit, but sent him among you for the profit of your souls. Therefore, love the Lord and receive baptism in his name, because the Lord our God has prepared for those who love him what the human eye has never seen and what has never entered the human heart (1 Corinthians 2:9).

Now turn away from [286] evil works and do good. Do not worship idols or sacrifice meat, because the Lord does not accept such things. In all matters, observe and do what our brother Boniface teaches you, and you will be saved—you and your children—forever.

Therefore, build a house in which your father himself may dwell, and churches in which you may pray, so that God may forgive your sins and grant you everlasting life.

## Another letter of Pope Gregory to the Saxons

**Pope Gregory to the entire people of the province of the Saxons.**
“‘I am a debtor both to the wise and to the foolish’ (Romans 1:14),” I confess, dearest ones, “desiring you to know what concern I have for you” (Colossians 2:1), and for those who have received the word of exhortation concerning the faith of Jesus Christ, and for those who are still to receive it, “that your hearts may be comforted, instructed in charity and in all the riches of the fullness of understanding, for the knowledge of the mystery of God the Father of Jesus Christ” (ibid., 2), as the outstanding Apostle says, “in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge” (ibid., 3). I say this [Col. 1152A] “because the kingdom of God is near” (Luke 21:31), so that “no one may deceive you any longer through subtle arguments” (Colossians 2:4), or so that you may seek your salvation in any metal by worshiping idols made by human hands—whether of gold, silver, bronze, stone, or made from any other material—which, under a false name, have long been called “gods” by the pagans, and in which demons are known to dwell. “For all the gods of the nations are demons” (Psalm 95:5), as the Prophet says; “but the Lord made the heavens” (ibid.).

But all among you who have received Christ our Lord should walk in him, rooted and built up in him and strengthened in faith, “abounding in thanksgiving. See that no one deceives you any longer through philosophy and empty deceit” (Colossians 2:6–8). For “the children [Col. 1152B] of darkness are wiser than the children of light” (Luke 16:8). Depart, children, from the worship of idols (1 Corinthians 10:14), and draw near to and worship the Lord our God, who made heaven and earth, the sea, and everything that is in them (Revelation 14:7); and your faces will not be put to shame. For there is one Lord of human beings, birds, four-footed animals, and fish, “who is blessed for ever and ever” (2 Corinthians 11:31).

Therefore strip off the old person and put on the new Christ, laying aside everything—anger, indignation, malice, blasphemy, and shameful speech. Do not let such things come from your mouths (Colossians 3:8–10). “Withdraw from the worship of idols,” for the day is already growing late. Do not be idle (Matthew 20:6), but rather perform good works, so that Christ may dwell in you. “Whatever you do, in word or deed [Col. 1152C], do everything in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, giving thanks to God the Father through him” (Colossians 3:17). Rejecting the way of paganism, know that you have God in heaven.

Devote yourselves to prayer (Acts 6:4), and lift your hearts to Christ, for great is our Lord, exceedingly worthy of praise, and terrible above all gods (Psalm 95:4), “who desires everyone to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth” (1 Timothy 2:4). I admonish you concerning this, brothers: if anyone among you wishes to turn to Christ, do not in any way prevent him, nor compel him to worship carved images, because Christ the Lord himself lives with God the almighty Father, in the unity of the Holy Spirit, for ever and ever. Amen.

Dearest ones, I have sent to you Boniface, a faithful minister and fellow servant, my brother and fellow bishop [Col. 1152D], for this very purpose: that he may learn what concerns you and comfort your hearts with a sure word of exhortation in Christ Jesus our Lord, so that, freed from diabolical deceit, you may deserve to be joined to the children of adoption and, delivered from eternal damnation, may possess eternal life.

## Another letter of the same pope to Bishop Boniface

To the most reverend and most holy brother Boniface, fellow bishop: Gregory, servant of the servants of God.

Moved by the concern of the charge entrusted to me, and also by the evangelical instruction that says, “Entreat the Lord of the harvest to send workers into his harvest” (Luke 10:2), we have therefore judged it appropriate to send your reverend fraternity, in imitation of the apostles, who, when commanded by the Lord, were instructed [Col. 1153A]: “Go and preach the Gospel of the kingdom; you have received without payment, give without payment” (Matthew 10:7–8), into the regions of the West, for the illumination of the Germanic people sitting in the shadow of death (Luke 1:79). We foresaw that you ought to bring back profit from there, like that servant who, in the business of the talent, as it is written, faithfully declares that he had done so for God, his future Creator.

Because we see that, through the gift of obedience, the ministry of the word is flourishing, and because we have heard, as you have reported, that through the proclamation of preaching an unbelieving people has been converted, we give thanks to the power of the Lord. We pray that he from whom every good thing proceeds (James 1:17), and who desires everyone to come to the knowledge of the truth (1 Timothy 2:4), may cooperate with you and, by the inspiration of his power, lead that people from darkness back to the light (1 Peter 2:9). For this reason [Col. 1153B] we believe that a rich reward is being credited to you in heaven by the almighty Lord (Matthew 5:12).

For if you persevere in the good struggle, you will be able to say with the Apostle: “I have fought the good fight, I have finished the course, I have kept the faith” (2 Timothy 4:7). But persist in your labor so that you may receive the crown. For God promises salvation at the end to those who persevere. Let neither threats terrify you nor fears cast you down; holding firm confidence in God, proclaim the word of truth. Completion will come through divine assistance, provided that the work is good in its intention.

Accordingly, we have learned from the text of your letters how many you have converted from error. We rejoice and, giving abundant thanks to God, exult in the profit of souls. Moreover, concerning that bishop who until now, through a certain indolence, had neglected to spread the word of preaching among the same people [Col. 1153C], and who now claims a portion of it for himself, as though it were his parish, we have written in a paternal letter to our most excellent son Charles, urging him to restrain that bishop; and we trust that he will order this to be prohibited. You, however, must not cease to preach what leads to salvation, “in season and out of season” (2 Timothy 4:2).

Accordingly, we have not neglected to write to the Thuringians and to the people of Germany about matters concerning the welfare and salvation of their souls, ordering among other things that they build bishoprics and establish churches. For he who does not desire the death of a sinner, but rather that he should turn and live (Ezekiel 33:11), will give growth to all (1 Corinthians 3:7).

May God keep you safe. Given on the day before the Nones of December, while our most pious lord Augustus, Leo, crowned by God, the great emperor, was reigning, in the eighth year; and also while Constantine [Col. 1153D], his son, the great emperor, was reigning, in his fifth year, in the eighth indiction.

## Letter of Pope Gregory to Bishop Boniface

To the most reverend and most holy brother Boniface, fellow bishop, sent by this apostolic Church of God for the illumination of the Germanic people and of the surrounding nations dwelling in the shadow of death (Luke 1:79), peoples established in error: Gregory, servant of the servants of God.

We experienced great rejoicing when, after reading the letters of your most holy fraternity and rereading their sequence, we found that, by the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, you had converted very many from paganism and error to the knowledge of the true faith. Since divine instruction teaches us through parables that the one to whom five talents had been entrusted gained another five (Matthew 25:20), we [Col. 1154A] applaud this profit of such an enterprise together with the whole Church.

For this reason we have sent you, by the authority of the blessed Apostle Peter, the gift of the sacred pallium, which you are to receive and put on; and, with God as author, we decree that you are to be counted among the archbishops. You will learn from the apostolic mandate how you are to use it: you are to wear it only when celebrating the solemnities of Mass or when it happens that you consecrate a bishop.

But because, by the grace of the Lord, you have brought crowds in those same regions over to the true faith, and because you cannot reach everyone in order to provide or explain to them what concerns salvation, now that the grace of Christ and its faith have spread far and wide in those regions, we command that, in accordance with the statutes of the sacred canons, where the multitude of the faithful has increased, you should, by the authority of the Apostolic See, ordain [Col. 1154B] bishops—yet with careful pastoral consideration, so that the dignity of the episcopate may not be cheapened.

You should know concerning the presbyter whom you said had come to us in the previous year and had, by our judgment, been released from his wicked actions: he made no confessions to us, nor was he absolved by us so that he might fulfill his own desires. If you find him devoted to error, we command you, by the authority of the Apostolic See, to correct and amend him according to the judgment of the holy canons, and to do the same with anyone else you may find in such a condition.

He said, “I am a presbyter,” and requested letters of recommendation to our son Charles. We granted him no other permission. If he behaves wickedly, we wish him to be avoided along with the others. Those whom you have claimed were baptized by pagans, if the matter is as reported, we command you to baptize again in the name of the Trinity [Col. 1154C].

Meanwhile, you have permitted some people to eat wild horses, and many others to eat domestic horses. Holy brother, do not allow this to happen again; rather, with God’s help, restrain it in every way possible and impose a fitting penance upon them. For it is unclean and detestable.

Concerning the dead, you are reported to have consulted whether it is permitted to offer oblations for them. The holy Church holds that each person may offer oblations for his genuinely Christian dead, and that a presbyter may commemorate them. Although we are all subject to sins, it is fitting that a priest commemorate and intercede for Catholic dead; nevertheless, he may not do such a thing for the impious, even if they were Christians.

We also command that those who are uncertain whether they have been baptized, or not, or who were baptized by a presbyter who sacrifices to Jupiter and eats sacrificial meat, be baptized again [Col. 1154D]. We decree that each person should observe his lineage up to the seventh generation. And, if you are able, take care that no man who has had two wives should marry another.

Concerning those who have killed their father, mother, brother, or sister, we decree that throughout their lifetime they should not receive the Lord’s Body except at the time of death, as viaticum. They should also abstain from eating meat and drinking wine, and should fast on the second, fourth, and sixth days of the week until the end of their lives, so that they may thereby wash away their committed crime.

You also said that, among other matters, some of the faithful sell their slaves to pagans for sacrifice [Col. 1155A]. We earnestly admonish you, brother, to correct this and not allow it to happen any longer. For it is a crime and an act of impiety. Therefore assign to those who have committed it the same penance as to a murderer.

Whenever you consecrate a bishop, let two or three bishops assemble with you, so that what is done may be pleasing to God; and when they have assembled and are present, perform the consecration.

We wish you, dearest brother, to observe these things carefully and to carry out with devoted piety the work of salvation that you have begun, so that, for the profit you have brought, you may receive a reward from the Lord our God in eternal blessedness. We have also sent the privilege, prepared according to your request, attached to this letter. We hope that, under the protection of the Lord our God, you may bring to Christ our God a complete and undiminished profit from the conversion of those who have gone astray [Col. 1155B].

May God keep you safe, most reverend brother.

## Here Gregory the First ends; from this point Gregory the Younger begins

Gregory, bishop and servant of the servants of God, to all the bishops dear to us, the venerable presbyters, and the religious abbots of all the provinces.

“While the Lord cooperates and confirms the word” (Mark 16:20), this most holy man Boniface, our brother and fellow bishop, who had been sent into those regions by our predecessor, Gregory of holy memory, to preach the word of God, has after a long time, with the Lord cooperating with his ardent desire, come to be presented, for the sake of prayer, at the sacred thresholds of the blessed chief apostles Peter and Paul [Col. 1155C]. After completing his prayer, he was released by us for the labor he had undertaken, with the angel of the Lord going before him.

Therefore, for the love of Christ, may all of you, in affection, reverence, and religious devotion, deign to provide him assistance [p. 287], remembering what our Lord Jesus Christ says: “Whoever receives a prophet in the name of a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward; and whoever receives a righteous person in the name of a righteous person will receive a righteous person’s reward” (Matthew 10:41).

And if perhaps any of your ministers wishes to join this most holy man in the ministry of exhorting people to the holy and Catholic faith, do not in any way prevent him, dearest ones. Rather, provide assistance and give him helpers from your flock who, by God’s grace, can sufficiently minister the word of preaching to the nations [Col. 1155D], so that they may win souls for our almighty God, and so that your community may receive a share in the good work and they may deserve to hear the Lord’s voice: “You who have left everything and followed me will receive a hundredfold and possess eternal life” (Matthew 19:29).

Farewell.

## Letter of Pope Gregory

Gregory, pope, to all the nobles and people of the provinces of Germany: the Thuringians, the Thesis, the Borthari, the Nistresi, the Unedredi, the Lognai, the Sudnodi, the Graffelti, and all those established in the eastern region.

Because our predecessor, Gregory, bishop of holy memory, moved by divine will to [Col. 1156A] make a people perfect for God (Luke 1:17), ordained and sent to you the bearer of this letter, Boniface, our most reverend brother and fellow bishop, teaching him the rule and standard of the apostolic and Catholic faith of the Roman Church, which, with God as its author, we serve; and because, after a period of time, he presented himself at the thresholds of the blessed chief apostles for the sake of prayer and now asks us to instruct him in matters concerning the salvation of souls, we, with God’s favor, instructing him as holy Scripture teaches, release him to return to you, dearest ones.

We exhort you in the Lord to receive worthily from him the word of exhortation, and to accept in the ministry of the Church the bishops and presbyters whom he ordains by the apostolic authority granted to him [Col. 1156B]. If he finds any who have strayed from the path of the true faith or from canonical teaching and prohibits them, do not in any way hinder him; rather, let them obediently accept, for God’s sake, whatever has been imposed upon them. For whoever proves rebellious against obedience acquires condemnation for himself.

You, dearest ones, who have been baptized in the name of Christ, have put on Christ (Galatians 3:27). Therefore abstain and keep yourselves from every pagan fault—not merely correcting yourselves, dearest ones, but also your subjects. Reject completely diviners and sorcerers, sacrifices for the dead or in groves, omens from springs, amulets, enchanters and poisoners—that is, practitioners of magic—and sacrilegious observances formerly customary in your territories. Turn with your whole mind to the Lord [Col. 1156C]; fear, worship, and honor him, sharing in the memorials of the saints, as the Apostle says (Romans 12:13).

For if your faith, as the Lord says, is like a mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, “Move,” and it will move (Matthew 17:19). For our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ says in his holy word: “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your strength” (Matthew 22:37). And again: “Whoever acknowledges me before human beings, I also will acknowledge before my Father who is in heaven” (Matthew 10:32). Therefore in another place he promised, saying: “Whatever you ask the Father in my name will be done for you” (John 14:13). And again: “Ask and you will receive; seek and you will find; knock and it will be opened to you. For everyone who asks receives, and whoever seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened” (Luke 11:9–10) [Col. 1156D].

And you, dearest ones, produce worthy fruits, so that on the day of the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ you may deserve to attain the heavenly dwellings.

Farewell.

## Another letter of blessed Pope Gregory

To the sons most dear to us who are established in the provinces of Bavaria and Alamannia: Juggo, Luidon, Ridolt, and Piphilo, Sevadas. Pope Gregory.

The authority of the Catholic Church and of the holy Fathers commands that synods should be held twice each year for the salvation of the Christian people and for the exhortation of the children of adoption, and that examination of canonical cases should take place, so that each person may be assisted through pious instruction as necessity requires [Col. 1157A].

Therefore, according to the Apostle’s teaching, I admonish and exhort you, dearest ones, by the mercy of God, to walk worthily of the calling to which you have been called (Ephesians 4:1), so that your ministry may be complete before God.

It is fitting that you know that you should receive the present brother and fellow bishop Boniface, who acts as our representative, with the worthy and proper honor due to the name of Christ. You should receive from him and faithfully retain the ecclesiastical ministry, with Catholic faith, according to the holy rule and custom of the Catholic and apostolic Church of God, over which, through God’s preceding mercy, we appear to preside, just as he was sent by us with apostolic authority.

Reject and exclude the pagan rite and teaching of visiting Britons, or of false and heretical priests [Col. 1157B], or of adulterers, wherever they may come from. Teach the people entrusted to you by God through pious admonitions, and avoid entirely sacrifices for the dead. According to what you have been taught by our aforesaid fellow priest, holding to Catholic and apostolic doctrine, hasten to please the Lord God and our Savior.

And wherever he orders you to assemble for the celebration of councils—whether by the Danube, or in the city of Augsburg, or wherever he judges appropriate—be found ready for the name of Christ. Thus we may learn, through his command, of your assembly, so that on the day of the coming of Christ Jesus we may deserve to stand with the fruit of good works before his tribunal, saying: “Behold, we and the children whom you have given us, Lord” (Hebrews 2:13); “we have not lost [Col. 1157C] any of them” (John 18:9).

And may you deserve to hear the Lord’s voice saying: “Come, blessed of my Father; receive the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world” (Matthew 25:34).

Farewell.

## Letter of the same to Boniface

To the most reverend and most holy brother Boniface, fellow bishop: Gregory, servant of the servants of God.

The religious presbyter Denual, sent by you, brought me welcome news when he reported that you were safe and that, by God’s favor, you were making progress in the ministry for which you were sent. He also delivered letters sent by you, in which you indicated that the Lord’s field, which had lain uncultivated and had bristled with the thorns of unbelief, had received the seed of the word when the ploughshare of your teaching broke through it, and had produced a fertile [Col. 1157D] harvest of faithfulness.

In the same letter you appended several questions, asking how this holy apostolic Roman Church holds and teaches these matters. You know well that the blessed Apostle Peter was the origin and beginning of the episcopate. In response to your consultation concerning the state of the Church—not from ourselves as though from ourselves, but by the grace of him “who opens the mouth of the mute and makes the tongues of infants eloquent” (Wisdom 10:21)—we tell you, according to the teaching of apostolic authority, how you ought to proceed.

First, it was asked at what degree of descent relatives may be joined in marriage. We say that, so long as they recognize themselves as related by kinship, they ought not to enter into such a marital union. But because moderation is preferable, especially in [Col. 1158A] so barbarous a people, to strict severity, it may be permitted for them to marry after the fourth generation.

You also stated that, if a woman, overcome by illness, is unable to render the marital due to her husband, what should her spouse do. It would be good if he remained in this condition, devoting himself to abstinence. But because this is a matter for the strong, the man who cannot contain himself should marry instead, while not withdrawing the assistance of support from the woman whom illness prevents, and whom no detestable fault excludes.

Concerning a presbyter, or any priest accused by the people: if there are no certain witnesses who can establish the truth of the charge brought against him, an oath should be required, and he should produce as witness the one to whom “all things are naked and open” (Hebrews 4:13), thereby remaining in his proper rank [Col. 1158B]. For a man who has been confirmed by a bishop must not be subjected to such a repetition a second time.

At the solemnities of Mass, what our Lord Jesus Christ gave to his holy disciples must be observed: “He took the cup and gave it to them, saying: ‘This is the cup of the New Testament in my blood; do this whenever you drink’” (Matthew 26:27–28). Therefore it is not appropriate to place two or three cups upon the altar when the solemnities of Mass are celebrated.

You consulted concerning sacrificial foods, asking whether they might be eaten by the faithful if the sign of the life-giving cross had been placed upon them. It is sufficient to answer with what the blessed Apostle says: “If anyone says, ‘This has been offered in sacrifice,’ do not eat it, for the sake of the one who indicated it and for the sake of conscience” (1 Corinthians 10:28).

You added further [Col. 1158C] that, if a father or mother commits a son or daughter, during the years of childhood, to the discipline of a monastery under a rule, whether it is permissible for them, after completing the years of puberty, to leave and marry. We absolutely reject this, because it is wrong that the reins of pleasure should be loosened for children whom their parents have offered to God.

You also acknowledged that some people had been baptized by adulterous and unworthy presbyters without the questioning of the creed. In these matters, your affection should retain the ancient custom of the Church: whoever has been baptized in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit (Matthew 28:19) may not be baptized again. For the gift of this grace was received not in the name of the baptizer but in the name of the Trinity. Let what the Apostle says be upheld: “One God, one faith, one baptism” (Ephesians 4:5) [Col. 1158D].

We command you to impart spiritual instruction to such people with particular care. Concerning children who have been taken from their parents and who do not know whether they have been baptized, reason requires that you baptize them according to the tradition of the Fathers, if there is no one who can testify.

But lepers, if they are faithful Christians, should be admitted to participation in the Lord’s Body and Blood; they should nevertheless be forbidden to celebrate the common rites with the healthy.

You also added that, if a pestilence or deadly disease has entered a church or monastery, those whom it has not yet touched flee from the place to avoid the danger. This seems foolish. No one can escape the hands of God.

At the end, the letter stated that certain presbyters or bishops are entangled in many [Col. 1159A] vices, and that their lives stain the priesthood within themselves. You asked whether you might eat or speak with them if they were not restrained. We say that, by apostolic authority, you should rebuke and admonish them and lead them back to the purity of ecclesiastical discipline. If they obey, they will save their souls, and you will have gained a reward. Nevertheless, do not refuse conversation and a common table with them. It often happens that those whom disciplinary correction makes slow to receive the rule of truth are led onto the path of justice by the regularity of banquets and gentle admonition.

You should observe the same principle with those nobles who provide you assistance.

These matters, dearest brother, are sufficient to have been written by us from the authority of the Apostolic See. For the rest, we implore the mercy of God: may he who caused you, by apostolic authority, to act in those regions in our place, and who predestined the lights of truth to shine through your mouth in that dark forest, grant the most merciful increase of his aid, so that you may receive rewards for the fruit of your work and find forgiveness of sins [Col. 1159B].

May God keep you safe, most reverend brother.

Given on the tenth day before the Kalends of December, while our most pious lord Augustus, Leo, the great emperor crowned by God, was reigning, in the tenth year of his reign, and also while Constantine, the great emperor, was reigning, in the seventh year of his reign, in the tenth indiction.

## Another letter of the same to Boniface

To the most reverend and most holy brother Boniface: Gregory, servant of the servants of God.

[Col. 1159C] The voice of the outstanding Apostle Paul, teacher of all the nations, says: “For those who love the Lord, all things work together for good” (Romans 8:28).

Therefore, recognizing in the words of your fraternity what you reported concerning the peoples of Germany—whom our God, in his mercy, has freed from the power of the pagans [p. 288] and whom, through your efforts and those of Charles, prince of the Franks, he has deigned to gather, numbering nearly one hundred thousand souls, into the bosom of the holy mother Church—and also recognizing what you have accomplished in the province of Bavaria, we raised our hands toward heaven and gave thanks to the Lord our God, the giver of all good things.

He opened in those western regions the door of mercy and compassion, the entrance to mercy, so that they might come to know the way of salvation, and sent his angel [Col. 1159D], who prepared your way before you (Malachi 3:1). To him be glory for ever and ever. Amen.

Since you reported that you had gone to the people of Bavaria and found them living outside ecclesiastical order, because they had no bishops in the province except one named Vivilo, whom we had previously ordained; and since, with the consent of their duke Otilo and of the nobles of that province, you ordained three other bishops and divided that province into four parts—that is, into four dioceses, so that each might have his own diocese—you acted well and with sufficient prudence, brother. Since you fulfilled the apostolic command in our place and acted just as we instructed you, do not cease, most reverend brother [Col. 1160A], to teach them the holy Catholic and apostolic tradition of the Roman See, so that the uneducated may be enlightened and may hold to the way of salvation by which they can attain eternal rewards.

As for the presbyters whom you found there, if it is unknown by whom they were ordained, and there is doubt whether those who ordained them were bishops: if the presbyters themselves are men of good conduct and Catholic faith, instructed in the ministry of Christ and in every holy law, and if they are suitable, let them receive from their bishop the blessing of the presbyterate, be consecrated, and thus exercise the sacred ministry.

Those who were baptized through the diversity and deviation of pagan languages, since they were nevertheless baptized in the name of the Trinity, ought to be confirmed through the laying on of hands and the anointing of sacred chrism.

[Col. 1160B] Bishop Vivilo was ordained by us. If he transgresses in any matter beyond the canonical rule, teach and correct him according to the tradition of the Roman Church that you received from us.

Concerning the council, we command your fraternity by apostolic authority to present yourself there in our place, so that you may celebrate it along the bank of the Danube. Insofar as the Lord gives you strength, do not cease to preach the word of salvation there, so that Christian religion may grow and multiply in the name of the Lord.

You will not have permission, brother, to remain in one place on account of the right of the labor you have begun. Rather, after strengthening the hearts of the brothers and of all the faithful who are uneducated in those western regions, do not cease to preach wherever the Lord opens the way of salvation to you. Wherever you find a place where it is necessary, according to canonical [Col. 1160C] rule, ordain bishops in our place and teach them to hold the apostolic and Catholic tradition.

By this you will prepare for yourself a great reward, because you will make a perfect people for our almighty God. Do not shrink, dearest brother, from undertaking rough and varied journeys, so that the Christian faith may be extended far and wide through your efforts. For it is written: “The way that leads to life is narrow and constricted” (Matthew 7:14).

Therefore perform the good work you have begun, so that on the day of Christ our God you may deserve to say, standing among the company of the approved holy Fathers: “Behold, I and the children whom you gave me; I have not lost any of them” (Romans 2:13). And again: “Lord, you entrusted five talents to me; behold, I have gained five [Col. 1160D] more” (Matthew 25:20).

Thus may you subsequently deserve to hear the Lord’s voice saying: “Well done, good and faithful servant; because you have been faithful over a little, I will set you over much. Enter into the joy of your lord” (ibid., 23).

May God keep you safe, most reverend brother.

Given on the fourth day before the Kalends of November, while our most pious lord Augustus Leo was reigning, in the twenty-third year of his reign, and also while Constantine, the great emperor and his son, was reigning, in the twentieth year of his reign, in the eighth indiction.

## Letter of Boniface to Pope Zacharias

To the most beloved lord, adorned with the insignia of the highest pontificate, an apostolic man, Zacharias: Boniface, servant of the servants of God.

[Col. 1161A] We confess, lord and father, that after we heard through messengers who brought the report that your predecessor in the apostolate, Gregory, bishop of the apostolic see, released from the prison of the body, had departed to the Lord, we heard no greater joy or greater gladness, and, raising our palms toward heaven, gave thanks to God than for the fact that the Most High Judge had granted your merciful Fatherhood to govern the canonical laws and hold the helm of the apostolic see.

I ask nothing otherwise than that, kneeling before your feet, we earnestly beseech you with our inmost prayers: just as we were devoted servants and obedient, submissive disciples of the piety of your predecessors by the authority of blessed Peter, so may we also merit to become obedient servants and submissive subjects of your piety under the canonical law. We desire to preserve and extend the catholic [Col. 1161B] faith and the unity of the Roman Church, and I do not cease inviting and inclining toward obedience to the apostolic see all hearers or disciples whom God may grant me in this mission.

We must also inform your Fatherhood that, by God’s grace, after the peoples of Germany had been somewhat struck or corrected, we ordained three bishops and divided the province into three parishes. We earnestly desire that those three towns or cities in which they have been established and ordained be confirmed and secured by written authority from you. We have decreed that one episcopal see should be in the castle called Vivozaburg, another in the town called Buraburg, and the third in the place called Erpesfryod, which formerly was [Col. 1161C] a city of pagan rustics.

We diligently request that these three places be strengthened and confirmed by a charter and by the authority of your apostolate, so that, if the Lord wills, by the authority and command of blessed Peter, three episcopal sees in Germany, founded and established by apostolic commands, may stand firm; and so that present or future generations may not presume either to corrupt the parishes or to violate the command of the apostolic see.

Let it likewise be known to your Fatherhood that Carloman, duke of the Franks, summoned me to him and asked me to begin and convene a synod in that part of the Frankish kingdom which is under his power. He promised that he wished to correct and amend something concerning ecclesiastical religion, which for a long time—that is, for no fewer than sixty or seventy years—had been trampled upon and dispersed [Col. 1161D]. Therefore, if, with God’s inspiration, he truly wishes to fulfill this plan, I ought to have and understand the counsel and command of your holy authority, that is, of the apostolic see.

For, as the elders say, the Franks have held no synod for more than eighty years, nor have they had an archbishop, nor have they anywhere established or renewed the canonical laws of the Church. Now, for the most part, episcopal sees throughout the cities have been handed over to laymen, greedy for possession, or to adulterous clerics, fornicators, and tax-collectors, for secular enjoyment. If, then, at the request of the aforesaid duke, I ought to undertake and command this business through your word, I wish to have at hand the command and judgment [Col. 1162A] of the apostolic see together with the ecclesiastical canons.

If I should find among them those whom they call deacons—men who from childhood have always led lives in brothels, always in adulteries, and always in every kind of uncleanness, and who came to the diaconate under such a reputation, yet now, while deacons, have four, five, or more concubines in bed with them at night, and nevertheless are neither ashamed nor afraid to read the Gospel and call themselves deacons—and if, in such incest, they proceed to the order of the presbyterate, discharge its office, claim to intercede for the people and offer sacred oblations, and finally, what is worse, having ascended through each rank under such reputations, are ordained and called bishops, I wish to have your authoritative command written down concerning what you decree about such men, so that, through an apostolic reply, sinners may be convicted and reproved.

Some bishops are also found among them who, although they say that they are not fornicators or adulterers, are drunkards, negligent, or hunters; others fight armed in the army and shed human blood with their own hands, whether of pagans or of Christians. Since I am recognized as a servant and legate of the apostolic see, and since there ought to be one word—mine here and yours there—if the judgment of your authority should require it, let us send envoys jointly.

Moreover, I must seek counsel and permission about one matter, because your predecessor of venerable memory, as you have heard, commanded me in your presence that, after my death, God willing, I should appoint a presbyter as my heir and successor in ecclesiastical ministry [Col. 1162C]. This pleases me, if it is God’s will, but now I am doubtful and do not know whether it can be done, because afterward that man’s brother killed the uncle of the duke of the Franks, and we still do not know how this discord can be reconciled and ended.

I beg that it be permitted by your authority for me, with the counsel of the servants of God, to do concerning this election what may seem jointly to us to be best for God, for the benefit of the Church, for spiritual fruit, and for the defense of religion; and that I may have your consent to do what seems best, which God may deign to inspire me to do. For this does not seem possible if the ruler should prove hostile.

Meanwhile I must seek and ask the counsel of your Fatherhood concerning a certain confusion and scandal in preaching which, when I recently came to you, disturbed your mind and brought shame upon the priests of the Churches. A certain layman of high rank came to us and said that he had been given permission by Gregory, bishop of the apostolic see and of holy memory, to take in marriage the widow of his uncle, who herself had been the wife of his cousin and had left him while he was alive. This man, who now desires to take her, claims that permission was granted to him. She is recognized as his relative in the third degree, had vowed chastity to God, had been veiled, and afterward, casting aside the veil, had married.

The aforesaid man claims that such a marriage was granted to him by the apostolic [Col. 1163A] see. We did not consider this true, because the synod and Church in which I was born and raised—that is, in transmarine Saxony, the Council of Lugdunum—was first established and ordered by disciples of Saint Gregory, namely the archbishops Augustine, Laurence, Justus, and Mellitus; and on the authority of holy Scripture they judged such a union and marriage to be a most grave crime, incest, a horrible outrage, and a damnable sacrilege.

Therefore, may your Fatherhood not disdain to indicate the truth of this matter to us, so that scandals, schisms, or new errors may not arise and grow from it among the priests of the Church or the Christian people.

For carnal and ignorant men—Alemanni, Bavarians, or Franks—if they see something being done near the city of Rome, suppose that the sins which we prohibit are permitted and granted by priests. While they count it as reproach against us, they take it as a scandal for their own lives. They claim that every year they have seen, in the city of Rome and near the Church of Saint Peter, when the Kalends of January begin, men leading dances through the streets by pagan custom, celebrating acclamations and sacrilegious songs in the manner of the gentiles, loading tables with food on that day or night, and refusing to lend anyone from their household fire, iron tools, or anything useful to a neighbor.

They also say that they have seen women there wearing amulets and charms in pagan fashion, tied around their arms and legs, and publicly offering them for sale, displaying them for others to purchase [Col. 1163C]. All these things, because they are seen there by carnal and foolish people, become for us here a reproach and an impediment to the completion of preaching and instruction.

The Apostle says of such things, rebuking them: “You observe days and seasons. I fear that I have labored among you in vain” (Psal. IV, 10, 11).

And Saint Augustine said:

“For whoever believes in the evils mentioned above—that is, in bodily signs, divine signs, haruspices, amulets, and any other kinds of omens—even if he fasts, even if he prays, even if he continually hastens to the churches, even if he gives abundant alms, even if he torments his little body with every affliction, none of this will benefit him so long as he does not abandon those sacrileges.”

For if your Fatherhood prohibits these pagan practices in the city of Rome, you will secure a reward for yourself and accomplish for us the greatest benefit [Col. 1163D] in ecclesiastical teaching.

There are also bishops and presbyters of Frankish origin who were adulterers and most notorious fornicators—men whom the sons born of their fornications accuse of adultery—who, returning from the apostolic see, say that the Roman pontiff gave them permission to exercise episcopal ministry in the Church. We argue against them, because we have never heard that the apostolic see judged contrary to the decrees of the canons.

We make all these matters known to you, dearest lord, so that we may give such men a response from your authority, lest, through the safeguard of your teaching, the sheep of the Church be led astray, but that the ravenous wolves, stirred up and overcome, may perish.

Meanwhile we have sent you small gifts [Col. 1164A], not because they are worthy of your Fatherhood, but as a token of charity and devoted obedience: one woollen article (vuillosam; the precise object is uncertain), and a very small amount of silver and gold. With the right hand of the Lord protecting you, we desire that your Blessedness may remain safe and prosper in Christ through length of days.

May the high-thundering God preserve you, rector of the apostolic see, in its holy sanctuary for long ages, pleasing to peoples throughout the world by your honey-sweet teaching; and may the gracious favor of Christ make you perfect and worthy of God. May the glorious and flourishing Mother bring your joys to completion, and may the house of the Lord rejoice in a fruitful people.

## Letter of Zacharias to Witta

To our dearest Witta, of the holy Church of Barbarana: Pope Zacharias.

[Col. 1164B] “The Lord working with them and confirming the word” (Mark XVI, 20) for the expansion of the law of Christianity and the path of orthodox faith, the most holy and reverend brother and fellow bishop Boniface made known to us that he had recently resolved and arranged to establish episcopal sees in the regions of Germany, where your Belovedness presides, and to divide the province into three parishes. When we learned this, with great exultation and our palms extended toward the stars, we gave thanks to the Enlightener and Giver of all good things, the Lord God and our Savior Jesus Christ, who “has made both one” (Ephesians II, 14).

The aforesaid most holy man requested from us in his letter that your sees be confirmed by apostolic authority. Therefore, with ardent heart, with divine assistance, and by the authority of blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, to whom God and our Savior Jesus Christ gave the power of binding and loosing [Col. 1164C] human sins in heaven and on earth (Matthew XVI, 19), we confirm and decree that your episcopal sees shall remain secure and firm. By the authority of that prince of the apostles, we forbid, from the present time and for future generations, that anyone should dare to act against this same arrangement of yours, which, by God’s favor, has been made among you at our command.

We further forbid that anyone should dare, according to the tradition of the holy canons, to transfer anyone from another episcopate to that place or to ordain a bishop there after your summons from this world, except one who has represented the office of our apostolic see in those regions [Col. 1164D]. Nor may one parish invade another’s boundaries or presume to take away its Churches.

For, which we do not believe, if anyone should attempt with reckless boldness to act against this command of yours, let him know that he is bound by the bond of anathema under God’s eternal judgment. But whoever observes the apostolic commands and attains the rule of right and orthodox faith shall receive the grace of blessing.

For the rest, we earnestly entreat the divine clemency to confirm and strengthen what the Lord has worked in you. May the charity of God, grace, and true peace be with your spirit.

Most holy and dearly beloved, strive with every effort for the faith of Christ and contend to complete his ministry, so that you may merit to say with the distinguished Apostle: “I have fought the good fight, I have completed the course, I have kept the faith. Henceforth the crown of righteousness is laid up for me, which the righteous Judge, the Lord, will award me on that day” (II Timothy IV, 8).

We desire, greeting you in the Lord, that you remain well. Farewell. Given on the Kalends of April, while the lord Constantine, great emperor, was reigning, in the twenty-fourth year, the second year of his empire, indiction six.

## Letter of Zacharias to Bishop Boniface

To the most reverend and most holy brother Boniface, fellow bishop: Zacharias, servant of the servants of God.

Virgil and Sodomus, religious men living in the province of the Bavarians, used their letters to inform us that your reverend [Col. 1165B] fraternity was ordering them to baptize Christians again.

When we heard this, we were greatly disturbed and fell into a certain astonishment, if the matter is as reported. They stated that there was a priest in that province who completely lacked knowledge of the Latin language and, when baptizing, unaware of Latin speech and mangling the language, said: “I baptize you in the name of the Fatherland (Patria), and of the Daughter (Filia), and of the Holy [feminine, sancta] Spirit.” On this account your Fraternity considered rebaptizing them.

But, most holy brother, if the man who baptized them did not introduce an error or heresy, but merely, through ignorance of Roman speech, mangling his language as we have said above, uttered these words while baptizing, we cannot agree that they should be baptized again. For, as your holy Fraternity knows very well, whoever has been baptized by heretics in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit must in no way be rebaptized, but must be cleansed solely through the imposition of hands.

Therefore, most holy brother, if the matter is as it has been reported to us, do not preach such things to them any longer; rather, let your Holiness strive to preserve what the holy Fathers teach and preach. May God keep you safe, most reverend brother. Given on the Kalends of July, while the most pious lord Constantine, Augustus, crowned by God, great emperor, was reigning, in the twenty-sixth year, the fourth year of his empire, indiction fourteen.

## Also, a letter of the same man to various bishops

To our dearest Regnifridus, bishop of Rouen; Rimbertus, bishop of Amiens; Deodatus, bishop of Beauvais; Helesaeus, bishop of Noyon; Fulciricus, bishop of Tongeren; David, bishop of Speyer; Ethereus, bishop of Châlons; Trenurardus, bishop of Cambrai; Burgardus, bishop of Würzburg; Genebandus, bishop of Laon; Romanus, bishop of Meaux; Agilolphus, bishop of Cologne; Heddo, bishop of Strasbourg; and the other most beloved bishops, presbyters, and also deacons, and all orthodox clerics of the Churches of God who hold apostolic teaching: Zacharias, endowed by divine grace, pontiff of the apostolic see and servant of the servants of God, sends greetings in the Lord.

[Col. 1166A] I give thanks to God the almighty Father, to the Lord Jesus Christ, his only Son, and to the Holy Spirit, who has deigned to inflame the hearts of all of you through the grace poured forth by him, so that you may walk in unity of faith and in the bond of peace, and so that “the splendor of the Lord our God may be upon us” (Psalm LXXXIX, 17), my beloved ones, with abundant grace of peace and charity. Thus may you be one body of your spiritual mother, the holy catholic and apostolic Church of God, over which, by God’s authority and ordering, although far unequal to such a height in strength, we preside, fulfilling the prophetic saying: “Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together” (Psalm CXXXII, 1).

Indeed, although we are absent in body because of the length of the journey, in the spirit of love we are always present with you, holding you in our inmost heart and praying continually that our God and Lord Jesus Christ may much more confirm [Col. 1166B] your hearts and strengthen you in the proclamation of the Gospel and in the ministry which you exercise. Thus may the people entrusted to you, through your pious admonitions and with God’s help, be liberated from the devil’s deceit and remain safe, and may you merit to bring profit from their souls on the day of Christ.

For it is written: “The children of wisdom are the Church of the just, and their nation is obedience and charity” (Ecclesiasticus III, 1).

I therefore beseech you, my dearest ones, to walk worthily of the calling by which you were called, as is fitting for saints, with great wisdom, bearing with one another in charity, eager to preserve the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace and charity (Ephesians IV, 13), because “the end of the commandment is charity from a pure heart and a good conscience and an unfeigned faith” (I Timothy I, 5).

I rejoice in you, beloved, because your faith and unity toward us are precious and manifest not only before God but also before all human beings, since with most benevolent will you have turned toward your helper and teacher appointed by God, blessed Peter, prince of the apostles. Your faith and good reputation are praiseworthy, because “you think the very thing that ought to be thought” (Romans XII, 3).

And now, with God cooperating, your holiness has been gathered into our fellowship in one pastoral sheepfold. We have one shepherd, instituted by the Shepherd of shepherds, the Lord God and our Savior Jesus Christ, as prince of the apostles and our teacher.

You therefore have, in our place, to confirm your love and labor with you in the Gospel, the most holy and reverend Boniface, our brother and archbishop, legate of the apostolic see and presenting our authority [Col. 1166D].

Let your steadfastness therefore stand against the contentions of those who think contrary things and not the things of God (Mark VIII, 33). Let your steadfastness be stronger than stone, as it is written: “Do not fear them, nor be terrified by the face of those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul.” “What you hear in the ear, preach in the light, fearing him who can destroy both body and soul and cast them into Gehenna” (Matthew X, 26, 28).

My brothers, although we walk in the flesh, we do not wage war according to the flesh. “For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but powerful through God for the destruction of strongholds, destroying counsels and every height that exalts itself against the knowledge of God, and bringing every understanding into captivity and leading every thought into obedience to Christ” (II Corinthians X, 4–5).

For the rest, brothers, be strengthened in the Lord and in the power of his might. May abundant peace and grace from God and our Lord Jesus Christ be ministered to you. We embrace and kiss your charity, as though present with you, in the unity of the Spirit, in the bond of the peace and charity of Christ. May God keep you safe, our dearly beloved.

## The same man to Boniface

To the most reverend and most holy brother Boniface, fellow bishop: Zacharias, servant of the servants of God.

[Col. 1167B] When the letters of your most holy Fraternity had been brought to us, and we had caused them to be read through one by one, we found in the sequence of your letters that, through the working of our sins, while you were laboring to cultivate the seeds of the Lord’s wheat in order to increase the spiritual crop, the enemy suddenly sowed weeds among them (Matthew XIII, 25), so as to hinder your Holiness in your good work.

But let your holy Fraternity persist without ceasing in prayer, together with the brothers who labor with you; and, constructing spiritual hoes, let it carry out the weeds after uprooting them, to be burned (ibid., 30), as blessed Pope Gregory said: “Let the good work be ours in intention; for through divine assistance it will be brought to perfection.”

Since these things are so, dearest brother, take courage in the Lord, and he himself will be your helper.

Concerning the incursion of the peoples that has occurred among your flocks, we are grieved; but let this adversity in no way disturb your Fraternity. The city of Rome too has often been depopulated by disasters that befell it, yet the Lord in his omnipotence has deigned to console it from above.

But preach to the peoples entrusted to you, most reverend [Col. 1167C] brother, fasting and litanies of supplication before the Lord, and his surpassing clemency will help you. As we have said, let adversity in no way disturb you. Do not in any way fail in the good work that you have begun.

As for us, although we are unworthy and sinners, by our prayers and those of our fellow priests, insofar as we can, we assist you.

Concerning the synod convened in the Frankish province through Pippin and Carloman, our most excellent sons, and carried out by you in our place according to the instruction of our letters, we have learned how you acted and have given thanks to our almighty God, who strengthened their hearts so that they might be helpers in this pious work. You accomplished everything excellently and canonically, both concerning false bishops, fornicators, and schismatics, and concerning the other so-called priests who acted against the institutions of the canons or against the catholic and apostolic Church of God. Concerning these matters, in accordance with your report, we reply point by point.

You reported that all the princes of the Franks had chosen a city joining all the Frankish territories as far as the borders of the pagans and extending into the regions of the Germanic peoples, where you had previously preached, so that you might have a metropolitan see there in perpetuity, from which you could instruct the other bishops in the way of righteousness and which your successors after you might possess by perpetual right. We receive this decision with joyful heart, since it has occurred by God’s will. Even if false priests and schismatics have tried to obstruct it, the Lord will scatter their vain struggle and will establish those things which agree with the ordinances of the holy Fathers.

Since the princes of the Franks themselves have also been helpers to you in this matter, may almighty God repay them with the reward of their service and bestow innumerable good things upon them.

Likewise, concerning that false bishop whom you said was the son of an adulterous cleric and a murderer, born in adultery, raised without discipline, and guilty of the other evils and horrors that you recounted individually—and who consequently consecrated priests like himself—your reverend Fraternity remembers that we have already written three times that no murderer, adulterer, or fornicator ought to usurp the sacred ministry, nor a penitent, nor anyone whom the sacred canons forbid to be a priest.

Concerning those baptized by him or the Churches consecrated by him, let your Fraternity inquire whether, while he was exercising the priesthood, he consecrated Churches in the name of the Trinity or likewise baptized children. If so, both the consecration of the Churches and the baptism of the children are to be confirmed.

You also reported that those priests whom you expelled publicly claim in the Frankish province that they have been absolved by us. Your holy Fraternity must not believe this in any way. For, if we had done what is impossible, we would have indicated it to your Charity through our letters.

But do not believe this impossible claim in any way. We neither preach one thing and do another, nor do we direct one thing while they chatter otherwise. With God’s help, we judge that what we preach must be observed to the very end.

We urge your Holiness most firmly to hold this: you must obey entirely the institutions of the holy Fathers and the decisions of the sacred canons, because we do not in any way preach one thing and do another.

As for your request that we write to the princes of the Franks [Col. 1168D], or to the other Franks, we wrote to them individually, as you requested, that they should be your friends and helpers in the Lord’s work.

Concerning the levy that you sought: since you could obtain from the Franks, for payment to churches or monasteries, no more than that twelve denarii be paid at the turning of the year by each union of servants, thanks be to God that you were able to obtain this; and may the Lord grant peace.

The lights of the saints are also increased because tribulation has now befallen the Saracens, Saxons, or Frisians, as you yourself informed us.

Concerning those who were deposed from the priestly rank for capital sins, after you found them adulterers and murderers, so that they could be neither priests [Col. 1169A] nor clerics, and who do not wish to be monks under penance, but go to the palace of the king of the Franks and ask him to grant them places in Churches or monasteries where they may live a lay life, thereby dispersing the sacred places: concerning this too we have sent instructions to the princes of the Franks about how it should be handled.

In another letter of yours we found contained everything that the false and schismatic bishops Aldebert and Clement had done against you. You indicated all their deeds and their most impious error individually.

We, having gathered our brothers and fellow priests, had the most wicked deeds of those evil men read aloud during their penance. When they had been reread before the council, all with pious zeal cried out with one voice that their schismatic doctrines, their most wicked traditions, and the most heinous life that Aldebert had caused to be written about himself should be burned in fire [Col. 1169B].

But we did not judge this right, because we ordered those writings to be preserved in the archive of the holy Church, either for safeguarding them or for condemning them eternally. They themselves received a fitting sentence, a copy of whose proceedings we have sent to your Holiness, brother, so that, when it has been reread in the Frankish province, every schismatic who hears how the holy catholic and apostolic Church of God judged the matter may recover from the perversity of his understanding.

In your third letter you informed us about another deceiver named Geolebo, who had formerly exercised the dignity of bishop, and because he hastened to us without consulting anyone. When he arrives, if it pleases the Lord, what is to be done will be done.

As for your Reverence, just as you have begun with the Lord’s help, we wish that, in our place, a council should be held every year at a suitable time in the Frankish province. Thus, through the attendance of priests and by means of the institutions of the sacred canons, no adverse thing will dare to spring up there; rather, with the unity of the Church of God, ecclesiastical discipline, and apostolic order being extended everywhere in those regions, all the multitudes of the peoples, even in the western parts, may be true Catholics and may no longer, entangled in errors through false priests, be plunged into destruction.

When you have convened the council, let your Fraternity hold conference with the metropolitans whom we have confirmed, concerning what you said: that no one should be received without letters of recommendation.

For this matter itself, and for all the princes of the Franks, we have sent letters of admonition, as we said above. Concerning that city which was formerly called Agrippina and is now called Cologne, at the request of the Franks we have confirmed by a command of our authority a metropolitan see in your name, and we have sent to your Holiness, for future times, the security of that same metropolitan Church.

May God keep you safe, most reverend and most holy brother. Given on the day before the Kalends of November, while the most pious lord Constantine, Augustus, crowned by God, great emperor, was reigning, in the twenty-seventh year, the fifth year of his empire, indiction fourteen.

## Also, a letter of Zacharias to Boniface

[Col. 1170A]

To the most holy and reverend brother Boniface, fellow bishop: Zacharias, bishop and servant of the servants of God.

Blessed is God the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who gathers what is scattered, preserves what is gathered, and increases faith and confidence in his servants for preaching the word of the Gospel of Jesus Christ our Lord, who lives with the same Father and the Holy Spirit in the unity of the ages of ages. To him be glory and praise; he is helper and protector of those who believe in him. For he himself said: “Whoever believes in me will live and will not die” (John VI, 47), because “I am the way, the truth, and the life” (John XIV, 6).

We praise and greatly exalt his holy name, joyful and rejoicing, through these bearers and through the letters of your holy Fraternity [Col. 1170B], learning that you survive in this life and are well in the Lord. We ask the immeasurable divinity of our God to preserve you for a very long time for preaching the Gospel and the sacrament of his holy faith, to fortify you with his protection, and in merciful goodness to guard you from the snares of adversaries.

Your holy Fraternity reported in its letter that our predecessor, Gregory of blessed memory, bishop of this holy apostolic see, when he sent your Fraternity to preach the word of the Gospel among the regions and pagan peoples of Germany, had strengthened you with a verbal promise, so that you might confirm still more firmly in the word of exhortation any orthodox bishops, presbyters, or others whom you were able to find, and communicate with them [Col. 1170C]—which was done.

But if you found any deceiving bishops, false presbyters, or others deviating from the straight path of faith, you were to have no communion with them.

You have confessed that, with God comforting you, you have observed this spiritually up to the present. Or, if, because of the influence and human favor of the Frankish people, when you physically approached them you were not wholly able to abstain, compelled by the necessity of the Churches of God, nevertheless your soul was not defiled by their council or by consenting to their communion.

Therefore, because you remained among them without consenting to their iniquity, this brings you no detriment before God. For, if they obeyed your preaching, they would be saved; but if they remain in their iniquity, they themselves will perish. You, however, in accordance with the prophet’s saying, “have saved your soul” (Ezekiel XXXIII, 9).

Concerning the bishops and the pallia of the Franks, you wrote that they have not yet fulfilled their promise. If they fulfill it according to their word, they will receive praise from it (Romans XIII, 3). But if they act otherwise, they will see to it themselves. For we, by the generosity of divine grace, “give freely what we have received freely” (Matthew X, 8).

Your benevolent intention in this matter has certainly been accepted by us.

You also requested that the monastery which is situated in an immense wilderness, in the midst of the peoples to whom you preach, founded by you and dedicated in honor of our God and Savior, where you have also arranged for monks to live under the rule of blessed Benedict, be fortified by the privilege of the apostolic see in your name [Col. 1171A]. Acquiescing in your wishes, we have arranged this according to your request and desire.

For it is fitting that an excellent preacher and minister of divine service should attain what he desires and bring the good work he has begun to completion, as it is written in the Lord’s command: “Whoever perseveres to the end will be saved” (Matthew X, 22). And: “Blessed is that servant whom, when the Lord comes, he finds doing this; for he will set him over all his goods” (Matthew XXIV, 46–47).

Meanwhile, your aforesaid messenger Lul, together with his other companions, made known more clearly everything that had been entrusted to them by your Fraternity, both orally and in writing [Col. 1171B]. We have sent our reply to your Fraternity concerning these matters, both orally and in writing.

For the chapters contained in the petition presented by them are appended below; concerning these you asked us which matters should be accepted and which rejected.

First, concerning birds—that is, jackdaws, crows, and storks—which Christians must altogether avoid eating, and also beavers, hares, and wild horses, which must be avoided even more strictly. Nevertheless, most holy brother, you are thoroughly versed in all the Holy Scriptures.

Concerning the Paschal fire, about which you inquired from the holy Fathers of old: since, by the grace of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, and by his precious blood, the Church was consecrated on the Thursday of Easter, while the sacred chrism is being consecrated, three large lamps of ample capacity shall burn continually, with oil collected from the Church’s various candles, in the more secluded part of the church, representing the inner tabernacle. They shall be watched and tended with great care, so that the oil itself may suffice until the third day. From these lamps, on Holy Saturday, the priest shall renew the fire taken for the baptismal water of the sacred font.

Concerning crystals, as you stated, we have no tradition.

You asked what should be done concerning those afflicted with the royal disease, whether they be horses. If people have had this disease from birth or by hereditary origin, they must be escorted outside the city; but they must not be prevented from receiving alms from the people. If, however, someone—whether great or small—should happen to be afflicted not from birth but by an illness that has subsequently arisen, he must not be cast out; rather, if possible, he must be cured. Nevertheless, when he comes into the church for communion, he shall enter to partake of the sacrament after all the others have been supplied.

Horses, however, that have been contaminated by the aforesaid disease, if they cannot be cured, must be thrown into wells and pits, lest the others be contaminated by the contagion of the same disease. As for animals that have been torn by raging creatures—that is, by rabid wolves and dogs—they must be separated from the others, lest the others be contaminated through the raging and biting animals. If there are only a few, they must, as we said above, be thrown into pits.

Your fraternity also asked whether holy women may wash one another’s feet, as men do, both on the Lord’s Supper and on other days. This is a commandment of the Lord, and whoever fulfills it through faith will receive praise for it. For men and women have one God, who is in heaven.

As for the blessings performed by the Gauls, as you know, brother, they vary in many errors. They do this not according to apostolic tradition, but out of empty glory, bringing condemnation upon themselves, since it is written: “If anyone proclaims to you a gospel contrary to what was proclaimed, let him be accursed” (Galatians 1:9).

You have received, dearest brother, the rule of Catholic tradition. Thus preach to all and teach all, just as you have received it from the holy Roman Church, which, by God’s authority, we serve.

You also asked whether it is permissible to ordain a priest before the age of thirty. It is good and appropriate, dearest brother, if it can be done and if suitable men can be found, that priests be ordained according to the provisions of the sacred canons from among men of mature age and good reputation. But if such men cannot be found and necessity requires it, levites and priests may be ordained from the age of twenty-five onward, as is contained in the law of the Lord.

Concerning Milo and others of his kind, who greatly harm the Churches of God, urge them to withdraw from such a wicked deed, in accordance with the Apostle’s words: “Preach the word; be urgent in season and out of season” (2 Timothy 4:2). If they heed your admonitions, they will save their souls. But if not, they themselves will perish, wrapped in their sins. You, however, who preach rightly, will not lose your reward.
