We must not plot against another what we would be unwilling to suffer, 32.

[Col. 1242] Magic is forbidden to clergy, 143. A magistrate serving as a duumvir must be restrained by the Church, 100. A greater cannot be judged by a lesser, 49. The penalty for one who kills another by sorcery, 99. The wicked continually afflict the just, 29. The wicked whose correction is despaired of must be avoided, 40. If a bishop sells the Church’s slaves, he must make good the loss to the Church from his own property, 146. The insane must not be received into the clergy, 234. Manichaeus and Marcion said that Christ, as far as the flesh was concerned, did everything in appearance, 202. How Manichaeans are to be received into the faith, 169. A manumission carried out by a bishop must not prejudice the Church, 146. Those directly and simply manumitted can be promoted to the clergy, 116. How the manumission of the Church’s slaves must be carried out, 116. A manumitted person ordained priest must make his former patroness his heir, 116. A bishop is sometimes permitted to manumit, 116. Pope Mark sent the bishops of Egypt a faithfully copied exemplar of the Council of Nicaea, 150. Pearls of the sacred mysteries must not be cast before swine, 10. Mary gave birth to God made flesh, 76. The agreement of the emperor Marcian and the Fathers of the Council of Chalcedon, 74. A husband or wife cannot be joined to another while the spouse is alive, 88. If a husband is aware of his wife’s adultery, 100. The edict of the emperor Marcian, 74. The words of the emperor Marcian concerning the Council of Chalcedon, 74. Marcian’s second sanction addressed to Palladius, 75. Preface of Martin, bishop of Braga, 141. Letter of Pope Martin to Amandus, 262. False martyrs must not be venerated, 68. No one ought to defame the dignity of martyrs, 76. The martyrs suffered because they confessed the true divinity and humanity in Christ, 193. Anathema upon one who condemns the veneration of martyrs, 63. The feast days of martyrs must not be celebrated during Lent, 143. The primacy of the city of Marseille, 91. How the marriages of freedmen are to be contracted, 127. Marriages between blood relatives must be prohibited by bishops, 30. One who stains marital fidelity through concubinage is to be deprived of communion, 105. Eutyches, who condemns marriage, is condemned, 63. Marriage must not be dissolved on account of religion, 63. No religion can dissolve a marriage, 278. The penalty for attempting marriage with two sisters, 144. A marriage is not duplicated if, after dismissing a female slave, one takes her as wife, 220. The bodily members do not have the same function, 152. There are two kinds of lies, 123. A lie must not be constantly present in one’s mouth, 6. The table of priests ought to have a reading, 109. It is execrable to have intercourse with a menstruating woman, 12. A prostitute coming to the faith is to be received, 100. In examining cases, a metropolitan must summon the provincial bishops, 24. There cannot be two metropolitans in the same province, 73. By whom a delinquent metropolitan is to be rebuked, 26. The office of the metropolitan in general councils, 1. A metropolitan must not usurp the proud title of supreme priest, 79. A metropolitan must not be negligent concerning heretical depravity, 88. A metropolitan of a neighboring province is to be summoned if the bishops disagree, 142. A metropolitan is to be established in every province, 2. A metropolitan must be designated in every province, 186. How the metropolitan is to be elected, 169. A soldier is proved by combat, 13. Our warfare must not be carnal, 14. One who accepts the belt of secular military service after the remission of sins must not be ordained, 171. Who ought to touch the sacred ministries, 143. The sacred vessels must not be carried into the field, 144. What sort of persons are to be initiated into the ministries of the divine table, 7. The penalty for transgressing the rules of the ministries, 144. Ministers of the altar must not attend frivolous spectacles, 68. A lesser must not rise up against a greater, 76. Mercy toward the poor enriches penance, 8. Human presumption must not measure the extent of God’s mercy, 219. Mass is to be said on the night of the Lord’s Nativity, 23. Masses in the province of Braga are to be celebrated in the same order, 139. At what time Mass is to be celebrated, 23. Masses must not be celebrated except in consecrated places unless necessity requires it, 263. The whole Mass is to be heard on Sunday, 96. The mystery of the Mass, begun by one person, may be completed by another, 120. The manner of burying the bodies of the dead, 110.

[Col. 1243] Communion must be denied to one who repeatedly commits adultery, especially after recovery from illness, 100. How one who commits adultery with a Jewess is to be punished, 101. What penalty is imposed on a husband aware of his wife’s adultery, 100. A nun must not be taken as a wife, 283. Clerical monks must persevere in their monastic commitment, 172. The penalty for monks and nuns who beget children, 166. A monk is made such either by paternal devotion or by his own profession, 115. Monks may be promoted to the sacred orders, 167. Wandering monks, even if they take wives, are to be brought back to the monastery, 115. Monks must not be enslaved by a bishop’s authority to servile duties, 115. One monk must not promote or retain with himself a monk from another monastery, 84. Monks must instruct nuns while avoiding intimate familiarity, 147. Monks or nuns must not summon lay persons to themselves, 76. A monk may not have an orarium in the monastery, 98. A monk must not abandon the cells of his brothers, 98. If a bishop has built a monastery, 127. Convents for girls are to be built farther away from monasteries of monks, 96. A new monastery cannot be founded without the bishop’s authority, 97. A bishop must not claim for himself what has been offered to monasteries, 103. A monastery of the Order of Saint Benedict is founded in Gaul through Boniface, the papal legate, 290. How one abandoning the monastic life is to be punished, 220. One who violates the monastic profession must be barred, 118. How one trained in monastic rules who comes to clerical office is to be admitted, 233. How those who have received penance at the point of death may communicate, 93. Offerings of those dying in penance without communion must not be received, 85, 94. The death of those who live piously must not grieve us, 176. Those who kill themselves, and those punished for their crimes, must not be given ecclesiastical burial, 139. We would not overcome the author of death and sin unless God had assumed our nature, 188. One near the ruin of death must not do penance without consulting the bishop, 100. The bodies of the dead must not be buried in the basilicas of the saints, 139. Women must not enter the altar, 68. A woman must not baptize, 3. Faithful women must avoid gatherings of strangers, 182. A woman sins by wearing men’s clothing, 63. Women from whom an evil suspicion could arise must not live with clergy, 79. The penalty for a woman who commits adultery until the end of her life, 100. Women are forbidden to live with clergy, 167. However learned a woman may be, she must not presume to teach men in an assembly, 83. The purification of a woman after childbirth, 280. The penalty for a woman who marries two brothers, 62. A woman who kills a fetus conceived through adultery must never be admitted to communion, 100. A woman must not enter the sacristy, 143. The penance of a woman who sins while professing devotion, 143. Bodily cleanliness must be maintained, 275. No one should be promoted for gifts but for merits, 118. A mute person can be baptized, 93.

N

One who does not truly honor Christ’s Nativity according to the flesh is a heretic, 98. No one in a village should celebrate the solemnity of the Lord’s Nativity or of Lent, 98. Human nature can merit nothing without God’s prior assistance, 177. Nature, deprived of heavenly support, can do nothing, 179. The two natures in Christ, 266. Those who kill born fetuses or induce abortion with drugs, 103. Negligence is the mother of ignorance, 9. The more negligent must be reconciled more slowly, 83. A niece must not be taken as a wife, 283. Those who do not know the things that belong to the Lord are unknown by the Lord, 86. The error of Nestorius and Eutyches, 257. Nestorius, saying that Mary was the mother of a mere man, is struck with anathema, 202. A neophyte in the faith must not readily be admitted to the clergy, 59. A neophyte must not be promoted, 67. Neophytes must not be appointed bishops, 84. How neophytes ought to live from the beginning, 83. A neophyte must not be ordained deacon or priest, 89. The canons of the Council of Nicaea may not be expounded according to private judgment, 177. Nothing is to be added to the canons of the Council of Nicaea, 199. Authentic Greek copies of the Council of Nicaea are requested by the Fathers of the Sixth Council of Carthage, 84; item 1 is vacant. When the names are to be recited, 170. The heretic Novatus is active in Africa, 34. How the Novatians are to be received, 127. The heretics Novatian and Nicostratus, 37. How Novatian is to be admitted to communion, 90. Novatians must not be received unless they have first renounced the heresy, 67. A stepmother or daughter-in-law must not be taken as a wife, 283.

[Col. 1244] How women who have been joined to Christ and violated their faith are to be admitted to penance, 272. A naked person cannot be stripped by any privilege, 23. Weddings must not be celebrated during Lent, 68. Weddings are to be praised, not condemned, 221. Wedding banquets must be free from shameful dances, 68. One who accuses weddings is anathema, 63. A priest must not be a guest at second weddings, 143. One joined in many marriages must do penance, 144. No one who has contracted a second marriage is to be admitted to the clergy, 234.

O

Offerings of those fostering hatred and quarrels must not be received, 132. The offering of children by their parents may be made up to what age, 129. Offerings made on the feasts of martyrs are to be divided equally among the clergy, 139. The offerings of the faithful must be divided into four parts, 234. The offerings of persons at odds must not be received, 83. The offerings of those departing this life in penance are to be received, 90. Of what the offering of bishops or priests at the altar is to be made, 2. Those who deny offerings for the dead to churches are to be excommunicated, 82. Slanderous attacks must be avoided, 32. Those who long cherish hatred and refuse to return to reconciliation are to be excommunicated, 96. Those who encourage hatred are homicides, 6. The suppression of the association of Octavius Ursio and others, 91. What is to be offered at the altar at the time of consecration, 2. What is forbidden to be offered at the altar, 2. Minor offices ought to prepare the way, 185. There should be one order for the morning and evening offices, 139. The works of the law do not justify, but the faith of Jesus Christ does, 9. This is the place for works; the future age is the time of rewards, 10. Prayer is to be offered with an upright face on appointed days, 143. We must pray that we may avoid foolish inquiries, 188. One must not pray with heretics, 68. The penalty for praying with an excommunicated person, 2. The penalty for praying with a condemned cleric, 2, chapter 12. A minister must not use an orarium, 68. The manner of wearing oraria, 114. The Lord’s Prayer is to be said every day, 113. The Lord’s Prayer must be recited by priests after Matins and Vespers, 102. The prayer to be said on the first, second, and third day of the council, 1. Vigilance must be maintained over prayer and communion, 2. We accomplish more through common prayers than through private ones, 174. An oratory may be established in the countryside to relieve the household’s fatigue, 95. An oratory must not be established without the bishop’s authority, 73. What kind of moral character those to be ordained ought to possess, 259. Those to be ordained must not be seditious, usurers, or avengers, 23. What kind of person one to be ordained ought to be, 213. What one to be ordained ought to promise, 133. Who may be ordained, 186. Unmarried men to be ordained must not have women to manage their household, 102. No one is to be ordained through another bishop, 60. Those ordained must obtain from the bishop letters of their ordination, 87. One who has accepted the belt of secular military service after the remission of sins must not be ordained, 168. How those ordained contrary to prohibition, or who beget children while in ministry, are to be punished, 91. Those ordained from the law courts or from military service must be deposed together with those who ordained them. Those ordained through deception are to be deposed, 85. Those ordained through bribery are to be removed from their order, 147. An ordained minister belongs where his ordination was performed, 88. An ordained man who cannot take possession of the church assigned to him must await the council’s decree, 142. An ordination performed by a bishop who is not the proper bishop is void, 142. How the ordination of a bishop is to be celebrated, 141. The ordination of bishops is to be carried out according to the circumstances of the places, 279. The ordination of a bishop must not be celebrated without the metropolitan’s authority, 66, 89, 141. Ordination must not be obtained by gifts, 140. One unworthy of the title of ordination does not deserve to be ordained, 73. Orders must not be conferred for a price, 132. The uneducated must not receive orders, 124. At what intervals of time the orders are to be conferred, 167. Orders must not be celebrated indiscriminately or at every time, 191. The order for promoting someone to the clergy, 182. The order of accusation, 15. The order for chanting the canonical hours, 96. The Orientals have been obstinate toward the Roman see from ancient times, 240. How a doorkeeper is ordained, 82. Doorkeepers must not remain away from the door for long, 140.

# Poems of the Carolingian Age

I.—Verses placed in praise of the Emperor Lothar at the front of the Gospel text that he himself presented to the monastery of Saint Martin of Metz, 1195.  

II.—Verses placed at the front of a Bible and written in golden letters in the most ancient manuscript codex of the monastery of Saint-Denis, which is now preserved in the Royal Library, 1197.  

III.—Verses written in golden characters at the front of a Bible in the most ancient manuscript codex of the Colbert Library, which belonged to Saint Stephen of Metz, 1199.  

IV.—On the death of Hugh, son of Charlemagne by a concubine-queen, 1205.  

V.—Epitaph of Clodarius, the boy king, 1207.  

VI.—Verses of an unknown poet on the order of the fellow-provincial bishops, 1208.  

VII.—Rhythmic verses on the destruction of the monastery of Glonn, 1212.  

VIII.—Verses on the battle fought at Fontenay, 1215.  

IX.—A Germanic poem, acclaimed for Louis, son of Louis the Stammerer, when he defeated the Northmen in the year 883, with a Latin translation by Johann Schiller, 1216.  

X.—Asclepiad verses with which the Gothic codex of Vigilanus, also called the Codex of Abelda, comes to an end, 1221.  

Faithful alphabetical index to Isidore Mercator, 122.
